oceanarray.pipeline.gridders.filters.filter_sigma_tukey(data: ndarray, window_samples: int, alpha: float = 0.5) → ndarray[source]

Apply a Tukey moving-average filter along axis=1 (time), NaN-aware.

Uses a finite-weight convolution: each output point is the weighted mean of the finite values within the window, so NaN gaps never contaminate adjacent points. Output is set to NaN where fewer than 10 % of the window weights are finite (edges of large data gaps).

Parameters:

  • data (np.ndarray) – 2-D array with shape (n_pressure, n_time). NaN marks missing values.

  • window_samples (int) – Length of the Tukey window in samples. Values < 3 or ≥ n_time return a copy of data unchanged.

  • alpha (float, optional) – Shape parameter of the Tukey window in [0, 1] (default 0.5). alpha=0 is a rectangular window; alpha=1 is a Hann window.

Returns:

Smoothed array with the same shape as data. Rows that are entirely NaN are returned unchanged.

Return type:

np.ndarray

Return the geometric tilt of an instrument dataset, in degrees.

tilt() of the dataset’s pitch and roll (a missing one counts as 0). An RDI ADCP (file_type == "rdi-raw" or a firmware_coordinate_system attr) records pitch as the raw tilt-1 reading; its true pitch is arctan(tan(tilt1)·cos(roll)) (RDI ADCP Coordinate Transformation manual), used here in place of the recorded pitch. Other instruments’ pitch is used as recorded.

history

The history attribute: each stage and reader appends one timestamped entry.

The history attribute: one timestamped entry per event, in one form.

Every stage and reader that records what it did appends to history through append_history(), so the timestamp format and the separator between entries live in one place.

oceanarray.history.HISTORY_SEPARATOR = '; '

Separates the entries of history; a note never contains it.

oceanarray.history.append_history(ds: Dataset, note: str) → None[source]

Append a timestamped note to ds.attrs['history'] in place.

The one place the history timestamp format and the "; " separator live, so every stage appends in the same form. A "; " inside note is cleaned to ", " (clean_history_note()) so the entry is read back whole.

Parameters:

  • note (str) – The event text, timestamped and appended.

oceanarray.history.clean_history_note(note: str) → str[source]

Return note without the entry separator, so it reads back as one entry.

history is read back by splitting on "; " (between entries) and then on the first ": " (time from text); a "; " inside a note would split it mid-sentence. Each one becomes ", ". Several events of one entry are joined with " | " instead.

Parameters:

note (str) – The event text.

Returns:

note with every "; " replaced by ", ", stripped.

Return type:

str

A double becomes float32 and a 64-bit integer int32 (when it fits), so a global attribute such as dp_dbar is not written at a precision its variable counterparts are not. Positions (latitude, geospatial_lat_min …) and anything not numeric are returned unchanged.

Return the first attribute (in name order) a product holds differently, or None.

Values are compared at the precision the writer stores them (same_attr()), so a float32 dp_dbar or a NaN position read back is not a change.

Parameters:

The attribute name, or None when all agree.

str or None

oceanarray.writers.dtypes.find_best_dtype(var_name: str, da: DataArray) → type[source]

Determine the optimal storage dtype for a variable.

Parameters:

  • var_name (str) – Variable name.

  • da (xr.DataArray) – Data array to inspect.

Returns:

Recommended numpy dtype.

Return type:

type

Notes

Rules applied in order:

  • String / datetime / timedelta / object variables: unchanged.

  • time in name: unchanged (preserve datetime64 / float encoding).

  • *_qc suffix or flag in name: int8.

  • latitude / longitude in name: float64.

  • Integer input: downsize to int32 if stored as int64, else unchanged.

  • float64 input: float32.

  • Anything else: unchanged.

name (str) – A variable or attribute name.

Returns:

True for a position.

bool

oceanarray.logger.attach_stage_handlers(log_file: Path | None) → list[Handler][source]

Attach a DEBUG file handler for a processing stage’s own log.

The stage log keeps the full DEBUG detail with the bare message. The console is configured separately (configure_console(), by the CLI or an API caller), so a stage does not add its own console handler and running one never doubles console output. Detach with detach_handlers().

Parameters:

log_file (pathlib.Path or None) – The stage log file; None attaches nothing.

Returns:

The handlers attached, for detach_handlers().

Return type:

list of logging.Handler

oceanarray.logger.configure_console(level: int | None = None) → Handler[source]

Attach a console handler (stderr, level-tagged) to the package logger.

The CLI calls this once so every command’s messages reach the terminal; the Python API configures logging itself (the library adds only a NullHandler). Progress goes to stderr so a command’s result on stdout stays pipeable. Idempotent: it replaces the console handler a prior call attached, so -q / -v can set the level without stacking handlers.

Parameters:

level (int, optional) – The console level; defaults to CONSOLE_LEVEL.

Returns:

The console handler attached.

Return type:

logging.Handler

oceanarray.logger.count_warnings(name: str) → Iterator[list[LogRecord]][source]

Collect the WARNING-or-worse records logger name logs in the block.

The records still go to every handler as usual; this only collects them, so a caller can count them. Records logged by child loggers are not included.

Parameters:

name (str) – Logger name, e.g. "oceanarray.pipeline.attribution".

Yields:

list of logging.LogRecord – The warnings so far; len() is their count.

Examples

>>> import logging
>>> with count_warnings("oceanarray.example") as warned:
...     logging.getLogger("oceanarray.example").warning("odd value")
>>> len(warned)
1
oceanarray.logger.deprecated_log_fn(log_fn: Callable[[str], None] | None) → AbstractContextManager[source]

Warn on a legacy log_fn and forward the package’s records to it in the block.

The public transform functions (to_canonical_units, interpolate_pressure, the ADCP-QC functions, …) used to take a log_fn callback. They now log through their module logger; this keeps a caller that still passes log_fn working for one release — every record is also handed to the callback — while raising a DeprecationWarning. A None callback warns nothing and forwards nothing.

Parameters:

log_fn (callable or None) – The legacy callback, called with each log message; None is a no-op.

Returns:

A context manager to wrap the function body.

Return type:

contextlib.AbstractContextManager

paths

Path resolution helpers for raw and processed directory trees.

Filesystem path and filename conventions for the oceanarray pipeline.

Single source of truth for folder resolution (Paths, read from a paths.yaml), the stage output-filename pattern, and turning instrument serial numbers into filename-safe tokens. Every processing stage derives its read/write locations from here so the logic is defined once rather than copied per stage.

Base URL of the hosted documentation, used in user-facing upgrade messages.

Raised when a directory uses the removed moor/proc (basedir) layout.

the keys of a paths.yaml and of each mooring’s entry under its moorings: section.

The folders a Paths holds

a mooring’s stack and grid in its directory, a site’s stack and grid (stackcat, gridcat) in the site’s.

class oceanarray.paths.Paths(yaml_dir: Path | None = None, raw_dir: Path | None = None, proc_dir: Path | None = None, report_dir: Path | None = None, export_dir: Path | None = None, caldip_dir: Path | None = None, moorings: Mapping[str, ~collections.abc.Mapping[str, ~pathlib.Path]]=<factory>, sources: Mapping[str, str] | None=None)[source]

Where a project’s files are: mooring YAMLs, raw files, processed files, pages, exports.

A mooring’s folder is <dir>/<mooring_name>, unless moorings gives that mooring an exact folder. A field left None is not given; a method that needs it raises MooringError naming the field. Paths are kept as given: a relative path stays relative to the current folder.

Parameters:

  • yaml_dir (str or Path, optional) – The folder holding the <mooring_name>.mooring.yaml files.

  • raw_dir (str or Path, optional) – The raw instrument files, one folder per mooring.

  • proc_dir (str or Path, optional) – The stage, stack and grid files, one folder per mooring.

  • report_dir (str or Path, optional) – The report pages, one folder per mooring.

  • export_dir (str or Path, optional) – The OceanSITES files (not per mooring).

  • caldip_dir (str or Path, optional) – The caldip outputs.

  • moorings (Mapping, optional) – Exact folders for moorings that differ, {mooring_name: {field: folder}} with fields from PATHS_FIELDS. Stored read-only.

  • sources (Mapping, optional) – Where each field set came from: "given" (the default), "standard" or "file". Not compared.

Raises:

ValueError – A moorings entry names a field not in PATHS_FIELDS.

Examples

>>> paths = Paths(raw_dir="raw", proc_dir="proc")
>>> paths.raw_mooring_dir("M2_2016").as_posix()
'raw/M2_2016'
>>> moved = paths.with_mooring("M2_2016", raw_dir="raw/M2_recovered")
>>> moved.raw_mooring_dir("M2_2016").as_posix(), moved.mooring_dir("M2_2016").as_posix()
('raw/M2_recovered', 'proc/M2_2016')
>>> Paths.standard("/data/OSNAP").mooring_dir("M2_2016").as_posix()
'/data/OSNAP/proc/M2_2016'
caldip_dir: Path | None = None
export_dir: Path | None = None

Instrument processing

stage 1 — standardisation

Convert raw instrument files (SeaBird, RBR, Nortek, RDI) to CF-NetCDF. Faithful to raw data; no QC.

Stage 1: raw instrument data → CF-NetCDF, faithful to the raw values.

stage1() takes raw datasets as read_mooring() returns them (stage=None) and applies stage 1’s transforms; it reads and writes no files. MooringProcessor reads each instrument’s raw file, calls stage1(), and writes <name>_<serial>_stage1.nc.

raw files

Find and read one instrument’s raw file as stage 1 does: the recovery-file naming convention for a missing filename, the Nortek header, and the calibration metadata only the raw header holds.

Find and read one instrument’s raw file, as stage 1 does.

A mooring YAML names each instrument’s raw file (filename, file_type, header_file); when it does not, the file is found from the instrument type and serial by the recovery-file naming conventions. The raw read also takes what only the raw file holds: the calibration coefficients in an SBE header and the Nortek pressure calibration and transformation matrix. Everything after the read is stage 1’s transform (oceanarray.pipeline.stage1.stage1()).

oceanarray.pipeline.raw_files.guess_instrument_filename(instrument_config: dict[str, Any], mooring_name: str, raw_mooring_dir: Path | None, input_dir: Path | None) → tuple | None[source]

Try standard recovery-file naming conventions to locate a raw data file.

Used when filename is absent or null in the mooring YAML. Searches {raw_mooring_dir}/{instrument}/ then {raw_mooring_dir}/.

Returns (filename, file_type, header_filename_or_None) when a candidate is found on disk, or None if no match is found (in which case a diagnostic message listing the paths tried is emitted via the package logger).

Naming conventions applied (all use the {serial}_recovery.<ext> pattern except ADCP):

  • microcat serial < 6000 → .asc / sbe-ascii (older SBE 37)

  • microcat serial ≥ 6000 → .hex / sbe-hex (newer SBE 37)

  • rbrsolo / rbrduet / seapoint → .rsk / rbr-rsk

  • aquadopp / nortek serial < 400000 → .dat / nortek-ascii + .hdr header file. nortek is accepted but deprecated; a warning is logged recommending aquadopp instead.

  • aquadopp / nortek serial ≥ 400000 → globs for converted_raw/A{serial}*/Average Velocity DF3.csv under the instrument directory, returns nortek-csv with the corresponding String Data.csv as the header path.

  • ADCP → tries {serial}_{mooring_name}_recovery.000 then {serial}_{mooring_prefix}_recovery.000 / rdi-raw

A trailing * or other non-alphanumeric annotation in the serial field is stripped before building the candidate filename.

stage 2 — trimming and clock correction

Trim to the deployment window; apply linear clock-offset/drift correction.

Stage 2: correct instrument clocks and trim each record to the deployment.

The correction is seconds added to instrument time (positive: the clock was slow). Three cases, from the mooring entry:

  • clock_offset only — a uniform constant shift throughout the record.

  • a recovery correction only — a linear ramp from 0 at deployment to that correction at recovery, from computer_clock_at_recovery / instrument_clock_at_recovery (computer − instrument), or from clock_drift_seconds.

  • both — the ramp runs from clock_offset at deployment to the recovery correction.

A pair read as unknown (or empty) gives no drift. The recovery correction is resolved by oceanarray.mooring.instruments.resolve_clock_correction(). A corrected file keeps time_orig and its history says what was applied; a file with no correction says why (no offset or reading, readings that agree, or time as delivered by the originator). The record is then trimmed to deployment_time … recovery_time.

oceanarray.pipeline.stage2.detect_deployment_window(ds: Dataset) → tuple[datetime64 | None, datetime64 | None, str][source]

Estimate the in-water window from a stage-1 pressure record, in the raw instrument clock.

Parameters:

ds (xarray.Dataset) – Stage-1 dataset with time (instrument clock) and pressure (dbar).

Returns:

(start, end, "pressure_pmin10dbar"), or (None, None, "no_pressure") without pressure, with under 10 records, or with no valid window. Add the YAML clock_offset for UTC.

Return type:

tuple of (numpy.datetime64 or None, numpy.datetime64 or None, str)

Notes

Threshold = 1st percentile of pressure in the middle 50 % of the records, minus 10 dbar: the middle excludes bench periods at either end, and a low percentile is not biased by knockdown (which inflates pmax). The start is the sample after the last one shallower than the threshold in the first 25 %; the end is the sample before the first one shallower in the last 25 % (else the last sample).

stage 3 — QC, rotation, and derived variables

Apply QC flags, rotate ADCP velocities to ENU, apply magnetic declination correction, and compute derived quantities (salinity, density, speed/direction).

Stage 3: pressure interpolation and QARTOD QC; writes _stage3.nc for every instrument.

Pressure is interpolated for instruments without it, or whose pressure the YAML marks bad (pressure_qc: 3 or more): from the nearest source within HAB_THRESHOLD, else bracketing sources above and below, else extrapolated (with a warning); flagged 8. Gross-range (parameters.QC_GROSS_RANGE, YAML qc_ranges) and spike (parameters.QC_SPIKE, qc_spike) tests follow, mooring-level YAML overridden by the instrument’s entry. Flags merge as 9 > 4 > 3 > 8 > 2 > 1, so interpolated pressure that fails a range test is 4.

oceanarray.pipeline.stage3.PROCESSING_LEVEL_QC = 'Ranges applied, bad data flagged'

QC tests applied and flagged, values kept; pressure taken from other instruments.

Type:

OceanSITES reference table 3 (processing_level) for what stage 3 did

Run Stage 3 QC and pressure interpolation for all instruments on a mooring.

caldip_dir is the entry point for the planned front-of-Stage-3 calibration-dip correction. It is not yet implemented (oceanarray.pipeline.calibration is a stub): supplying it logs a warning and continues, so the science data is unchanged, but each output stamps a caldip_applied attribute recording that only the stub ran, so the first real correction is visible as a change in that attribute. A caldip request also reprocesses existing _stage3.nc outputs (like force) so the marker reaches every instrument, not only freshly-written ones. None (the default) leaves the output exactly as before.

oceanarray.pipeline.pressure.compute_adcp_bin_pressure(ds: Dataset, lat: float, log_fn: Any = None) → Dataset[source]

Add bin_pressure(time, N_BINS) (dbar): transducer pressure plus the bins’ tilt-reduced range.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – Stage-3 ADCP dataset with pressure(time) (dbar, at the head), range(N_BINS) (m, from the transducer face) and orientation in orientation_yaml or orientation_instrument.

  • lat (float) – Latitude (decimal degrees north), for gsw.p_from_z.

  • log_fn (callable, optional) – Deprecated (removed in 0.7.0): configure logging instead.

Returns:

ds with bin_pressure; its tilt_correction is "applied", "none (firmware bin mapping)", "none (firmware config unknown)" or "none (pitch/roll unavailable)". Unchanged without pressure or range, or with an originator bin_pressure.

Return type:

xarray.Dataset

Raises:

MooringError – Orientation is not "up" or "down".

Notes

Offset per bin is gsw.p_from_z(-range_eff, lat), added for "down" and subtracted for "up". range_eff = range * cos(θ), with θ = arccos(cos(P_true) cos(roll)) and P_true = arctan(tan(tilt1) cos(roll)) (RDI Coordinate Transformation manual §4.2, Eq. 8): the beam-mean, first-order correction. It is applied only when the firmware config is known and is not earth coordinates with bin mapping (which already place the bins); NaN pitch/roll gives NaN bin_pressure. p_from_z is measured from the sea surface, not from the head: ~2–3 dbar at 300 m range from a 500 m transducer.

Must be called after apply_beam_to_enu (east/north/up_velocity must exist). No spike test is applied to velocity (burst-mode Aquadopps generate false positives at every burst boundary).

The single owner of QC-flag metadata: call this wherever a _qc variable is created or updated so the CF flag attributes cannot be forgotten. oceanarray.pipeline.qc.unify_velocity_qc(ds: Dataset) → Dataset[source]

Unify ENU velocity QC flags so all three components share the worst flag.

After gross-range, up-velocity propagation, and tilt QC, each component may carry different flags. A large east/north velocity flags only that component; tilt flags all three; up-velocity flags east and north but not itself from the east/north gross-range test. This function computes the element-wise worst flag across east_velocity_qc, north_velocity_qc, and up_velocity_qc, then writes that combined flag back to all three. The result: masking on any single component produces an identical, consistent velocity mask.

Adds east/north/up_velocity, current_speed and current_direction and sets coordinate_system = "ENU"; no-op for ENU input; refuses (no rotation) for "UNK". Needs heading, pitch, roll. Rotates vectors only: bins keep their nominal range (the depth tilt correction is oceanarray.pipeline.pressure.compute_adcp_bin_pressure()).

oceanarray.pipeline.coordinate.apply_declination_to_enu(ds: Dataset, lat: float, lon: float, latlon_source: str = 'unknown', log_fn: Any = None) → Dataset[source]

Rotate ENU velocities from magnetic to true north, in place.

u_true = u cos D + v sin D, v_true = -u sin D + v cos D (D positive east). No-op without east/north velocity, or when magnetic_declination or originator_magnetic_declination shows it was applied.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – Dataset to rotate (also returned).

  • lat (float) – Deployment latitude, for the magnetic declination.

  • lon (float) – Deployment longitude, for the magnetic declination.

  • latlon_source (str, optional) – Where lat/lon came from (an unknown position is detected and recorded).

  • log_fn (callable, optional) – Deprecated (removed in 0.7.0): configure logging instead.

Return type:

xarray.Dataset

oceanarray.pipeline.coordinate.xyz_to_enu(vx: ndarray, vy: ndarray, vz: ndarray, heading_deg: ndarray, pitch_deg: ndarray, roll_deg: ndarray, declination_deg: float = 0.0) → tuple[ndarray, ndarray, ndarray][source]

Vectorised XYZ → ENU rotation per Nortek Support reference script.

R = H @ P where (with hdg = heading - 90 + declination):

H = [[cos(hdg), sin(hdg), 0], [-sin(hdg), cos(hdg), 0], [0, 0, 1]]
P = [[cos(p), -sin(p)*sin(r), -cos(r)*sin(p)],
     [0,       cos(r),        -sin(r)],
     [sin(p),  sin(r)*cos(p),  cos(p)*cos(r)]]

The -90 offset accounts for the Nortek Aquadopp instrument frame where heading=90° aligns X→East, Y→North (standard geography at zero tilt). Magnetic declination is added to convert magnetic heading to true north.

Returns (east, north, up) arrays of the same shape as the inputs.

Calibration-dip correction, applied at the front of Stage 3 (see Calibration — applying caldip corrections at the front of Stage 3). Reading a caldip cast, finding the dips and reducing a dip to an offset or slope are implemented; applying still raises NotImplementedError.

Calibration-dip corrections at the front of stage 3 (reading and reduction only, so far).

caldip writes one {cast}_caldip.nc per cast, comparing instruments with a CTD at bottle stops. caldip reads a cast, dips finds each end’s file, stops reduces a dip to an offset or slope per variable; apply_caldip() (combining and applying) still raises NotImplementedError. *_diff is instrument − CTD, so corrected = measured − diff. See docs/source/methods/calibration.rst.

Read caldip’s per-cast netCDF: the bottle-stop comparisons a calibration correction is built from.

caldip compares each mooring instrument with the shipboard CTD at the bottle stops of one cast and writes {cast}_caldip.nc (dimensions instrument and stop). caldip measures; oceanarray decides: this module only reads and checks a cast. Choosing stops, reducing them to an offset or a slope, pairing a deployment dip with a recovery dip and applying the result are done elsewhere in oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.

A cast is refused, never applied, when it

  • carries a schema_version other than SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION,

  • lacks any of REQUIRED_PROVENANCE_GLOBALS,

  • has a units string on a temperature, conductivity or pressure variable that is not a recognised spelling of oceanarray’s canonical unit for that quantity, or

  • has two instruments whose serials are the same join key.

Sign convention: every *_diff variable is instrument − CTD, so an instrument is corrected toward the reference by subtracting it (corrected = measured − diff).

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.caldip.CALDIP_FLAGS_USABLE = (1, 3)

The flag values whose stops a correction may use.

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.caldip.CALDIP_FLAG_FLAGGED = 3

the stop’s difference exceeds caldip’s acceptance threshold (flagging_threshold, e.g. 0.005 °C). The comparison itself is sound — a stop that reads off is exactly what a correction is for — so it is usable for a correction.

Type:

caldip’s flagged

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.caldip.CALDIP_FLAG_OK = 1

Integer value meaning “ok” in caldip’s *_flag variables. flag_meanings order is ok no_data flagged missing unknown = 1 2 3 4 9.

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.caldip.read_caldip_cast(path: str | Path) → Dataset[source]

Open one {cast}_caldip.nc, check it, and return it ready for matching.

The file is loaded into memory and closed. The serial coordinate is replaced by its join key (canonical_serial()), and the units of every temperature, conductivity and pressure variable are rewritten to oceanarray’s canonical spelling. A genuine conversion (factor ≠ 1) multiplies the values and records units_converted_from and units_conversion_factor on the variable, as the stage writers do. The source path is recorded in attrs["source_path"].

Parameters:

The cast, with dimensions instrument and stop.

xarray.Dataset

  • CaldipProvenanceError – If any of REQUIRED_PROVENANCE_GLOBALS is missing.

Examples

Not run as tests: they need a caldip cast file on disk.

>>> cast = read_caldip_cast("proc_calib/msm142_2026/castM4_caldip.nc")
>>> instrument_record(cast, "013840")["cond_diff"].values

Find a mooring’s calibration dips: the caldip file for each end, and which end a cast is.

The mooring YAML names the cast for each end of the deployment:

caldip:
  deployment: {cruise: msm142_2026, cast: castM4}
  recovery:   {cruise: odb2026, cast: castX}

so a mooring whose two dips were processed on different cruises resolves both. A mooring with one dip is an ordinary case. caldip never pairs dips; this module does, from the YAML.

The two ends of a deployment, as the YAML names them, and the role each dip plays.

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.dips.cast_time(cast: Dataset) → Timestamp[source]

Return the time of a cast: the middle of its bottle stops.

Parameters:

cast (xarray.Dataset) – A cast from read_caldip_cast().

Returns:

The midpoint of the earliest and latest stop times.

Return type:

pandas.Timestamp

Reduce one dip’s bottle stops to the number a correction applies, per variable.

caldip gives, for each instrument and bottle stop, the instrument and CTD values and their difference (instrument − CTD). This module chooses which stops count and reduces them to one offset — or, for conductivity, one Sea-Bird AN31 slope — per dip. Combining the two dips of a deployment and applying the result happen elsewhere.

Two schemes (the mooring YAML caldip.scheme):

standard

temperature: the offset at the deepest usable stop; conductivity: the AN31 slope through the origin over the deep, stable stops; pressure: the mean offset at the stops near the deployment pressure.

rapid

reproduces the RAPID MicroCAT processing: temperature and conductivity offsets averaged over a deep pressure interval after interpolating the stop differences onto a 20-dbar grid; pressure interpolated to the deployment pressure, refused when that is deeper than the cast.

Every function works on one instrument’s record (instrument_record()) and returns a Reduction — with value NaN and a reason when the dip cannot give one.

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.stops.DEEP_STOP_DBAR = 500.0

stops deeper than this count when at least two qualify …

Type:

Conductivity slope, standard

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.stops.PRESSURE_WINDOW_DBAR = 200.0

stops within this distance of the deployment pressure are averaged; with none, the single nearest stop is used (provisional).

Type:

Pressure, standard

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.stops.RAPID_EXTEND_DBAR = 100.0

RAPID holds the deepest stop’s difference constant this far below it.

Type:

rapid

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.stops.RAPID_GRID_DBAR = 20.0

the pressure grid the stop differences are interpolated onto.

Type:

rapid

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.stops.RAPID_INTERVAL_DBAR = 500.0

default width of the deep averaging interval, ending at the deepest stop (provisional; RAPID set it by hand, e.g. 3500–5050 dbar at 26°N).

Type:

rapid

class oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.stops.Reduction(variable: str, kind: str, value: float, rule: str, stop_pressures: tuple[float, ...]=(), n: int = 0, sigma: float = nan, residual: float = nan, reason: str = '', source_tracking_id: str = '', extra: dict = <factory>)[source]

One dip’s correction for one instrument variable.

Parameters:

  • variable (str) – "temperature", "conductivity" or "pressure".

  • kind (str) – "offset" (subtract it) or "slope" (multiply by it).

  • value (float) – The offset (variable units, instrument − CTD) or the slope (dimensionless); NaN when the dip gives none.

  • rule (str) – The rule that produced it, in words, for the provenance attributes.

  • stop_pressures (tuple of float) – CTD pressure (dbar) of each stop used.

  • n (int) – Number of stops used.

  • sigma (float) – Standard error of a slope (NaN for an offset, or a slope from one stop).

  • residual (float) – RMS of β − slope·α over the stops used (NaN for an offset).

oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.stops.through_origin_slope(alpha: ndarray, beta: ndarray, weights: ndarray | None = None) → tuple[float, float, float][source]

Return the Sea-Bird AN31 slope β ≈ s·α, its standard error and the RMS residual.

s = Σ w·α·β / Σ w·α²; with r = β − s·α, σ_s = √(Σ w·r² / (n − 1) / Σ w·α²) (NaN for one point).

Parameters:

  • alpha (numpy.ndarray) – Instrument values (AN31’s α).

  • beta (numpy.ndarray) – Reference values (AN31’s β).

  • weights (numpy.ndarray or None, optional) – Per-point weights; equal weights when None.

Returns:

(slope, sigma, rms_residual).

Return type:

tuple of float

Examples

The bottle example in Sea-Bird Application Note 31:

>>> s, _, _ = through_origin_slope(
...     np.array([4.63421, 3.25349, 3.16777]), np.array([4.63481, 3.25398, 3.16822])
... )
>>> round(s, 6)
1.000138
oceanarray.pipeline.calibration.stops.usable_stops(record: Dataset, variable: str) → ndarray[source]

Return a mask of the stops usable for one variable.

A stop is usable when its difference and CTD pressure are finite and its caldip flag says the comparison exists: ok — and, in a schema-1 cast, also flagged, which there only means the instrument reads off by more than caldip’s acceptance tolerance (what a correction is for). no_data, missing and unknown stops are not used. Whether the water at a stop was stable enough is decided separately (stable_stops()).

Parameters:

  • record (xarray.Dataset) – One instrument’s record, indexed over stop.

  • variable (str) – "temperature", "conductivity" or "pressure".

Returns:

One entry per stop.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray of bool

Add the standalone ADCP flags on (time, N_BINS); none is merged into another.

east/north/up_velocity_qc are gross range on the value; percent_good_qc is 4 below prcnt_gd_bad and 3 below prcnt_gd_suspect; error_velocity_qc is 4 where |error_velocity| exceeds error_vel_threshold.

xarray.Dataset

Notes

RDI percent good has four columns; only column 3 (4-beam solutions) measures quality (the mean of all four is ~25 % for perfect data). Fewer columns: their mean is used; a percent_good on (time, N_BINS) is used as it is.

stamp

Mark stage files written before the processing_stage marker existed (oceanarray stamp FILE... --declare N).

Mark stage files written before the processing_stage marker existed.

Stage files now carry a processing_stage attribute; a file written before it existed is read with a WARNING and its stage inferred from the filename. stamp writes the marker into such a file, declaring the stage its name already states, so later reads are quiet. Only the two global attributes processing_stage and history are touched; the data, coordinates and encodings are left as they are. It never relabels a file: a stage that contradicts the filename, or a marker already present with another value, is refused.

oceanarray.pipeline.stack.stack(datasets: dict[str, Dataset], mooring_dict: dict | None = None, *, mooring: dict | None = None, dt_seconds: int | None = None, omitted: list[str] | None = None, stage2_reason: str = 'no stage-3 file', mask_flags: Iterable[int] | Mapping[str, Iterable[int]] | None = None) → Dataset[source]

Stack a mooring’s instruments onto a common time axis.

Pure function over datasets: no file I/O. The time axis runs through the deployment window in steps of dt_seconds, starting at the first whole multiple of the step (UTC, counted from 1970-01-01; on the hour at 3600 s). Each step takes every instrument’s nearest sample within ±dt/2 (no interpolation or averaging in time); a step with no sample in that window is NaN, so an instrument sampling slower than the step leaves the steps between its samples empty (with a warning). ADCPs expand into one level per bin plus a head level; a bin is at its own depth (water depth less its hab), and one at or above the surface is left out. Instruments marked stack: false are left out and named in instruments_excluded; instruments that cannot be stacked (no hab in the mooring YAML, non-canonical units, low-passed data) are left out and named in instruments_omitted. A level whose stage-3 magnetic_declination is "UNK" (no mooring position) gets NaN in the per-level magnetic_declination, whose comment names those levels.

Every value is kept, flagged or not, with two flag sets beside it from the same sample: ours (<var>_qc) and the originator’s translated to our table (<var>_qc_originator_mapped). A level with a value but no flag variable gets 0 (not QC’d); a step with no value gets 9 (missing). Each level records its originator dictionary (<var>_flag_translation, _counts; "none" without originator flags). The rule for what the pages hide and the grid leaves out (mask_flags) is recorded as stack_mask_flags; the potential density and tilt_from_pressure use only values it does not hide.

Parameters:

  • datasets (dict of str to xarray.Dataset) – Stage-3 (or stage-2) datasets keyed by cleaned serial.

  • mooring_dict (dict) – The loaded mooring YAML: the deployment window is the time axis, and each entry’s hab and stack flag are used. Each instrument’s sampling interval is detected from its time axis.

  • dt_seconds (int or None, optional) – Spacing of the common time axis, in seconds. None takes stack: dt_seconds from mooring_dict, else parameters.STACK_DT_SECONDS (3600).

  • omitted (list of str or None, optional) – Instruments the caller already dropped (e.g. unreadable files), recorded in instruments_omitted with the ones dropped here.

  • stage2_reason (str, optional) – Why any stage-2 datasets were stacked, recorded in stage2_reason and shown in the report’s amber note (e.g. "stage 3 failed in this run").

  • mask_flags (iterable of int, or Mapping of str to iterable of int, optional) – The flags hidden from the pages and left out of the grid (oceanarray.mask_rules.resolve_mask_flags()); None takes stack: mask_flags from mooring_dict, else parameters.MASK_FLAGS (4).

  • mooring (dict, optional) – Deprecated name of mooring_dict; removed in 0.8.0.

Returns:

The stack on (time, N_LEVELS), deepest level first.

Return type:

xarray.Dataset

Raises:

oceanarray.exceptions.MooringError – If the mooring YAML has no deployment window, the window holds no whole step, the time step is not a whole number > 0, or no instrument can be stacked.

oceanarray.pipeline.stack.stack_stale_reason(stack_path: Path, inputs: Mapping[str, Path], mooring_dict: Mapping | None = None, mooring_dir: Path | None = None, *, mooring: Mapping | None = None, dt_seconds: int, mask_flags: Iterable[int] | Mapping[str, Iterable[int]] | None = None) → str | None[source]

Return why the stack at stack_path must be rebuilt, or None when it is current.

The stack is current when the stage files it would be built from are the ones it records (same files, same SHA-256), the mooring YAML’s settings that shape it are the ones it records (deployment_settings without the grid’s settings and mask_flags), its mooring-level attributes and deployment window match the mooring YAML, and the same oceanarray release built it (the commit is ignored).

Parameters:

  • stack_path (pathlib.Path) – The existing <name>_stack.nc.

  • inputs (Mapping of str to pathlib.Path) – The stage file each instrument would be stacked from, keyed by serial.

  • mooring_dict (Mapping) – The loaded mooring YAML.

  • mooring_dir (pathlib.Path) – The mooring’s processing directory (stage-file paths are recorded relative to it).

  • dt_seconds (int) – The time step the new stack would use.

  • mask_flags (iterable of int, or Mapping, optional) – The rule the call gives (None: the mooring YAML’s or the default); a different rule from the one recorded rebuilds the stack.

  • mooring (Mapping, optional) – Deprecated name of mooring_dict; removed in 0.8.0.

Returns:

The first reason found, in words, or None.

Return type:

str or None

class oceanarray.pipeline.grid.MooringGridder(*, proc_dir: str)[source]

grid(mooring_name: str, p_start: float | None = None, p_end: float | None = None, dp: float | None = None, force: bool = False) → bool[source]

Interpolate the stacked mooring dataset onto a regular pressure grid.

Reads {mooring}_stack.nc, interpolates all variables onto a pressure axis from p_start to p_end in steps of dp dbar (each defaults to GRID_PMIN_DBAR, GRID_PMAX_DBAR, GRID_DP_DBAR in oceanarray.config.parameters), and writes {mooring}_grid.nc.

Returns True on success, False on error.

oceanarray.pipeline.grid.grid(ds_stack: Dataset, *, pmin: float | None = None, pmax: float | None = None, dp: float | None = None, mask_flags: Iterable[int] | Mapping[str, Iterable[int]] | None = None, slope_angle: float | None = None) → Dataset[source]

Interpolate a mooring stack, or a site stack, onto a regular pressure grid.

Pure function: no file I/O. At each time step every variable is interpolated linearly in pressure from the instruments with valid pressure and values onto pmin:dp:pmax dbar, with no extrapolation. The stack keeps every value; the values its rule hides (stack_mask_flags, default 4) are left out first, a value when its <var>_qc or <var>_qc_originator_mapped is in the rule (the velocity group also by velocity_flag and the ADCP seabed, percent-good and error-velocity flags). mask_flags may add flags for the grid, never drop one the stack hides.

A site stack (oceanarray.pipeline.concat.concat() output) is gridded one mooring per profile: at each step only the levels of the deployment deployment_index names; the overlap block is not gridded, and turnarounds stay empty. Its grid also carries deployment_index and the DEPLOYMENT record.

Parameters:

  • ds_stack (xarray.Dataset) – The stack, as oceanarray.pipeline.stack.stack() returns it, or a site stack.

  • pmin (float or None, optional) – The pressure grid, in dbar; default parameters.GRID_PMIN_DBAR, GRID_PMAX_DBAR and GRID_DP_DBAR. Recorded as pmin_dbar, pmax_dbar and dp_dbar.

  • pmax (float or None, optional) – The pressure grid, in dbar; default parameters.GRID_PMIN_DBAR, GRID_PMAX_DBAR and GRID_DP_DBAR. Recorded as pmin_dbar, pmax_dbar and dp_dbar.

  • dp (float or None, optional) – The pressure grid, in dbar; default parameters.GRID_PMIN_DBAR, GRID_PMAX_DBAR and GRID_DP_DBAR. Recorded as pmin_dbar, pmax_dbar and dp_dbar.

  • mask_flags (iterable of int, or Mapping of str to iterable of int, optional) – The grid’s own rule (see oceanarray.mask_rules.resolve_mask_flags()), which must hide at least what the stack’s does; default the stack’s rule. Recorded as grid_mask_flags.

  • slope_angle (float, optional) – Deprecated and ignored: the Grid cat report chooses the rotation (rotate_to=). Removed in 0.7.0.

Returns:

The gridded product on (time, pressure).

Return type:

xarray.Dataset

Raises:

  • oceanarray.exceptions.MooringError – If the stack has no pressure variable.

  • ValueError – If mask_flags is invalid or drops a flag the stack’s rule hides.

OceanSITES export

oceanarray.export(mooring_path, paths) (oceanarray export) writes a mooring’s stage-3 files and grid as OceanSITES 1.4 files; see OceanSITES export. to_oceansites is the conversion it uses, for a dataset already in hand; it writes nothing.

The export verb: a mooring’s stage-3 files and grid as OceanSITES 1.4 files.

oceanarray.pipeline.export.export(mooring_path: str | PathLike | None = None, paths: Paths | None = None, *, array_path: str | PathLike | None = None, grid: bool = True, overwrite: bool = False, dry_run: bool = False, mooring: str | PathLike | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, mooring_dir: PathLike | None = None, out_dir: PathLike | None = None, array: str | PathLike | Mapping | None = None) → list[Path][source]

Write a mooring’s stage-3 files and grid as OceanSITES 1.4 files.

Each instrument’s stage-3 file becomes a deployment data file and the grid a gridded file (see oceanarray.pipeline.oceansites.to_oceansites()). An instrument whose stage-3 file is missing or cannot be converted is reported and left out; the others are written.

Parameters:

  • mooring_path (str or os.PathLike) – The *.mooring.yaml; it must carry platform_code.

  • paths (oceanarray.Paths) – Where the files are: the stage-3 files and grid in paths.mooring_dir(name), the OceanSITES files written to paths.export_dir.

  • array_path (str, os.PathLike or None, optional) – The *.array.yaml; supplies site_code and project.

  • grid (bool, optional) – Also write the grid, when <name>_grid.nc exists (default True).

  • overwrite (bool, optional) – Replace files that exist (default False).

  • dry_run (bool, optional) – Convert but write nothing; return the paths that would be written.

  • mooring (str or os.PathLike or Mapping, optional) – Deprecated name of mooring_path; removed in 0.8.0.

  • mooring_dir (os.PathLike, optional) – Deprecated folders (out_dir default <mooring_dir>/oceansites), used when paths is not given; removed in 0.8.0.

  • out_dir (os.PathLike, optional) – Deprecated folders (out_dir default <mooring_dir>/oceansites), used when paths is not given; removed in 0.8.0.

  • array (str, os.PathLike or Mapping, optional) – Deprecated name of array_path (it also takes the parsed array YAML); removed in 0.8.0.

Returns:

The files written, instruments first, then the grid.

Return type:

list of pathlib.Path

Raises:

  • oceanarray.exceptions.MooringError – If the mooring YAML cannot be loaded, a folder is missing from paths, or nothing could be exported.

  • oceanarray.pipeline.oceansites.OceanSitesError – If the mooring YAML has no usable platform_code or deployment code.

  • TypeError – paths is not an oceanarray.Paths, or array_path is a mapping.

Examples

Not run as tests: they need a mooring YAML and its files on disk.

>>> import oceanarray as oa
>>> paths = oa.Paths.from_file("paths.yaml")
>>> oa.export(paths.mooring_path("M2_2016"), paths, array_path="OSNAPeast_2016.array.yaml")

Converting stage-3 datasets and grids to OceanSITES 1.4 datasets.

to_oceansites() returns one instrument’s stage-3 dataset as an OceanSITES deployment data file (OceanSITES Data Format Reference Manual 1.4, §4.1) and a mooring’s grid as a gridded file (§4.2): variables on (TIME, DEPTH), <PARAM>_QC flags from reference table 2, a data mode per variable (reference table 4) and the global attributes of §2.2. It writes nothing; the oceanarray.export() verb finds a mooring’s files, converts them and writes each under oceansites_filename().

oceanarray.pipeline.oceansites.DATA_MODES = ('P', 'D')

Data modes this package can claim (reference table 4); R is real-time telemetry, which a recovered instrument never is.

exception oceanarray.pipeline.oceansites.OceanSitesError[source]

Raised when a dataset or mooring YAML cannot make a valid OceanSITES file.

oceanarray.pipeline.oceansites.PARAMETER_CODES: dict[str, str] = {'conductivity': 'CNDC', 'current_direction': 'CDIR', 'current_speed': 'CSPD', 'dissolved_oxygen': 'DOX2', 'east_velocity': 'UCUR', 'north_velocity': 'VCUR', 'pressure': 'PRES', 'salinity': 'PSAL', 'temperature': 'TEMP', 'turbidity': 'TURB', 'up_velocity': 'WCUR'}

oceanarray registry name → OceanSITES parameter code (reference table 6), the inverse of the reader’s table so reading and writing share one mapping.

oceanarray.pipeline.oceansites.QC_FLAG_VALUES = array([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9], dtype=int8)

5 (value_changed), the originator’s QC modified the value; 6 unused.

Type:

Reference table 2 as oceanarray carries it, with its one extension

oceanarray.pipeline.oceansites.to_oceansites(ds: Dataset, mooring_dict: Mapping | None = None, *, array_dict: Mapping | None = None, stack: Dataset | None = None, source_file: str | None = None, mooring: Mapping | None = None, array: Mapping | None = None) → Dataset[source]

Return a stage-3 or grid dataset as an OceanSITES 1.4 file.

A stage-3 dataset (one instrument, a time dimension) becomes a deployment data file (manual §4.1); a grid (time × pressure) becomes a gridded file (§4.2, content type GRD).

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – A stage-3 dataset for one instrument, or a mooring’s grid.

  • mooring_dict (Mapping) – The loaded mooring YAML; supplies platform_code, deployment_code (default: YYYYMM of deployment_time), the position, the ships and cruises, and each variable’s data mode.

  • array_dict (Mapping or None, optional) – The parsed *.array.yaml; site_code and project are taken from it when present. Without site_code the attribute is left out.

  • stack (xarray.Dataset or None, optional) – For a grid: the stack it was made from, whose instruments are listed in history as the grid’s source files (§4.2.1).

  • source_file (str or None, optional) – Name of the input file, recorded in history; defaults to the file the dataset was opened from.

  • mooring (Mapping, optional) – Deprecated name of mooring_dict; removed in 0.8.0.

  • array (Mapping, optional) – Deprecated name of array_dict; removed in 0.8.0.

Returns:

Dimensions TIME, DEPTH, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE; each parameter on (TIME, DEPTH); id is the file name without .nc. A deployment file carries <PARAM>_QC and a data mode per variable.

Return type:

xarray.Dataset

Raises:

OceanSitesError – If platform_code is missing or holds _, the deployment code is not YYYYMM, a data mode is invalid or unearned, or the instrument has no type code.

clock offsets

Clock offsets and lag correlation across a mooring’s instruments.

Clock offset analysis functions for oceanographic instrument data.

This module provides functions to analyze and detect clock offsets between different instruments on the same mooring by comparing deployment timing and performing lag correlation analysis.

Naming conventions updated from the original module: - YAML key instruments → clamp - file suffix _raw → _stage2

deployment window

When each instrument entered and left the water, from its temperature record.

When each instrument entered and left the water: find the deployment window from temperature.

oceanarray.analysis.clock.deployment.compute_threshold_sigma_band(time, temp, sea_mean, sea_std, *, band_sigma=3.0, min_band_halfwidth=0.1, warm_side='auto', hours=24.0, smooth_window=9, warm_percentile=90)[source]

Decide a single threshold using sigma-band logic.

  • Band half-width = max(band_sigma*sea_std, min_band_halfwidth).

  • If warm_side == “high”: threshold = sea_mean + half_width (deep is below threshold) If warm_side == “low” : threshold = sea_mean - half_width (deep is above threshold) If warm_side == “auto”: infer ‘high’ vs ‘low’ from early/late warm percentiles.

Returns:

  • threshold (float)

  • deep_is_below (bool) – True if ‘deep’ should be considered <= threshold, False if >= threshold.

oceanarray.analysis.clock.deployment.likely_at_bottom_window(time: ndarray, strategy: str = 'fixed_hours', *, bottom_margin_hours: float = 24.0, bottom_inner_fraction: float = 0.25, deployment_time: datetime64 | None = None, recovery_time: datetime64 | None = None, deployment_margin_hours: float = 2.0) → tuple[datetime64, datetime64][source]

Return (bot_start, bot_end): the window where the instrument is almost surely at depth.

Strategies:

  • 'fixed_hours': [tmin + margin, tmax - margin]

  • 'percent_span': [tmin + f, tmax - f] using the inner fraction (e.g. 25 %)

  • 'deployment_bounds': [deploy + 2 h, recover - 2 h]

oceanarray.analysis.clock.deployment.likely_at_surface(time: ndarray, temp: ndarray, sea_mean: float, sea_std: float, *, hours: float = 24.0, smooth_window: int = 9, dwell_seconds: int = 1800, tol_sigma: float = 2.0) → tuple[datetime64 | None, datetime64 | None, float][source]

Return (sink_time, float_time, threshold). - sink_time: first sustained entry into ‘sea’ regime found in the early window. - float_time: last sustained exit from ‘sea’ regime found in the late window. - threshold: separator between warm and sea (midpoint between sea_mean and estimated warm_mean).

Configuration

parameters

Global processing parameters (QC thresholds, grid defaults, file paths, variable registry).

Package-level defaults for oceanarray: what the mplstyle cannot express.

Matplotlib appearance lives in the vendored report.mplstyle (MPLSTYLE). Values are read at call time, so reassigning one overrides it globally:

from oceanarray.config import parameters as params
params.DOWNSAMPLE_SECONDS = 60
oceanarray.config.parameters.CALDIP_METHODS: tuple[str, ...] = ('mean', 'ramp', 'slope')

How the two dips combine (mean, ramp) or, for conductivity only, a slope.

oceanarray.config.parameters.CALDIP_SCHEMES: tuple[str, ...] = ('standard', 'rapid')

The correction schemes a user chooses between; standard is the default.

oceanarray.config.parameters.CALDIP_TARGETS: tuple[str, ...] = ('temperature', 'conductivity', 'pressure')

The variables a caldip correction applies to.

oceanarray.config.parameters.CALDIP_USE: tuple[str, ...] = ('both', 'pre', 'post')

Which dips an override may keep.

oceanarray.config.parameters.CLOCK_DRIFT_OUTLIER_SECONDS: float = 120.0

A recovery clock drift further than this (seconds) from the median of the other instruments on the same mooring is reported by the mooring check: a mistyped reading (a wrong minute is 60 s) is likelier than one clock drifting that far from the rest.

oceanarray.config.parameters.CMAPS_BY_VARIABLE: dict[str, str] = {'absolute_salinity': 'YlGnBu_r', 'conservative_temperature': 'RdBu_r', 'current_speed': 'plasma', 'dissolved_oxygen': 'RdYlGn', 'dissolved_oxygen_2': 'RdYlGn', 'dissolved_oxygen_ml_l': 'RdYlGn', 'dissolved_oxygen_ml_l_2': 'RdYlGn', 'east_velocity': 'RdBu_r', 'error_velocity': 'RdBu_r', 'n2': 'plasma', 'north_velocity': 'RdBu_r', 'oxygen_saturation_pct': 'RdYlGn', 'potential_density': 'BuPu', 'potential_temperature': 'RdBu_r', 'salinity': 'YlGnBu_r', 'temperature': 'RdBu_r', 'turbidity': 'YlOrBr', 'u': 'RdBu_r', 'up_velocity': 'RdBu_r', 'v': 'RdBu_r', 'w': 'RdBu_r'}

Colormap lookup derived from VARIABLES — single source of truth so the two cannot drift. Excludes entries where cmap is None.

oceanarray.config.parameters.CONCAT_DEPTH_MATCH: str = 'depth'

match levels by depth (water depth − hab) within this many metres. Both can be set per mooring in stack:.

Type:

Default depth-matching rule for concat

oceanarray.config.parameters.GRID_DP_DBAR: float = 20.0

used when neither the call (or –dp) nor the mooring YAML’s grid: dp gives one.

Type:

Spacing of the grid levels, in dbar

oceanarray.config.parameters.GRID_PANEL_ROW_IN: float = 2.5

Height (inches) of one gridded-section / time-series panel row at full width. Matches the per-row height of the two-row “velocity at depth” figure (5” / 2), so stacked grid panels and single-row section figures share one scale and do not render over-tall.

oceanarray.config.parameters.GRID_PMAX_DBAR: float = 1000.0

used when neither the call (or –pmax) nor the mooring YAML’s grid: pmax gives one.

Type:

Deepest level of a mooring grid, in dbar

oceanarray.config.parameters.GRID_PMIN_DBAR: float = 200.0

used when neither the call (or –pmin) nor the mooring YAML’s grid: pmin gives one.

Type:

Shallowest level of a mooring grid, in dbar

oceanarray.config.parameters.INSTRUMENT_FAMILIES: dict[str, str] = {'adcp': 'adcp', 'aquadopp': 'point_velocity', 'currentmeter': 'point_velocity', 'microcat': 'hydrography', 'rbrduet': 'hydrography', 'rbrsolo': 'hydrography', 'sbe16': 'hydrography', 'sbe56': 'hydrography', 'thermistor': 'hydrography', 'tr1050': 'hydrography'}

Which instruments may share a depth across deployments in a concatenated stack. A temperature-only logger is hydrography, so it can sit in one depth with a CTD of another year. ADCP bins (and the ADCP head) are their own family, matched within half the bin size; an unlisted type is a family of its own. Keys are lower-case instrument types.

oceanarray.config.parameters.LINE_CMAPS_BY_VARIABLE: dict[str, str] = {'east_velocity': 'Blues_r', 'north_velocity': 'Blues_r', 'pressure': 'Blues_r', 'salinity': 'YlGnBu_r', 'temperature': 'RdBu_r', 'up_velocity': 'Blues_r'}

Colormaps for colouring lines (one per instrument, deep-first) — distinct from the pcolormesh field maps in CMAPS_BY_VARIABLE, because a field map that is fine for a filled panel can be wrong for overlaid lines (e.g. a diverging map’s pale midpoint washes lines out). Sampled deep→shallow with washed-out colours skipped by luminance (see oceanarray.plotters.helpers.ordered_line_colors()). Directions are chosen so the deepest instrument gets the darkest/most-saturated colour: temperature blue(cold/deep)→red(warm/shallow); pressure dark→lighter blue (bathymetry convention, deep = dark); salinity starts at the blue end.

oceanarray.config.parameters.MASK_FLAGS: tuple[int, ...] = (4,)

Flags whose values the figures and pages do not show and the grid leaves out, unless the call, --mask-flags or the mooring YAML’s stack: mask_flags says otherwise: bad (4) only. Display metadata for each physical variable.

Each entry has:

label

human-readable name for plot titles and legends.

units

udunits-2 / CF-compliant ASCII units for NetCDF attributes (e.g. "degree_Celsius"). The display unit for an axis label is derived from this through vunit() / vlabel() (degree_Celsius → °C) — there is no separate label_units column, so the display spelling cannot drift from the stored one.

standard_name

CF standard name. None when no standard name exists (e.g. turbidity in NTU, which has no udunits-2 unit).

cmap

default matplotlib colormap name, or None for variables without a natural diverging / sequential convention.

valid_min / valid_max

CF valid_min / valid_max attributes written to NetCDF output (physically valid range). Present only where a physical limit is known, with its source in a comment; absent for other variables (QC_GROSS_RANGE is for flagging only).

oceanarray.config.parameters.VAR_COLORS: dict[str, str] = {'absolute_salinity': '#E69F00', 'conductivity': '#44AA99', 'conservative_temperature': '#56B4E9', 'current_speed': '#D55E00', 'depth': '#000000', 'dissolved_oxygen': '#332288', 'dissolved_oxygen_2': '#332288', 'dissolved_oxygen_ml_l': '#332288', 'dissolved_oxygen_ml_l_2': '#332288', 'east_velocity': '#D55E00', 'n2': '#000000', 'north_velocity': '#0072B2', 'oxygen_saturation_pct': '#332288', 'potential_density': '#009E73', 'pressure': '#000000', 'salinity': '#E69F00', 'temperature': '#56B4E9', 'turbidity': '#661100', 'u': '#D55E00', 'up_velocity': '#CC79A7', 'v': '#0072B2', 'w': '#CC79A7'}

One colourblind-safe colour per variable, for single-instrument panels where each variable is drawn as one line (not the multi-instrument stack, which uses LINE_CMAPS_BY_VARIABLE). Physics use the Okabe-Ito palette (Wong, Nature Methods 8:441, 2011); biogeochemistry uses the Paul Tol palette. Look up with var_color() (single fallback, no scattered literals). Mirrors ctdcast’s VAR_COLORS.

oceanarray.config.parameters.VAR_COLOR_DEFAULT: str = '#000000'

Colour for a variable with no VAR_COLORS entry — one canonical fallback so callers don’t scatter their own literal defaults (which drift).

oceanarray.analysis.hydrography.calc_psal(ds: Dataset) → Dataset[source]

Compute Practical Salinity from conductivity, temperature, and pressure.

Uses the Gibbs SeaWater (GSW) toolbox: gsw.SP_from_C applies the PSS-78 equation to derive Practical Salinity (dimensionless, roughly PSU) from conductivity (mS cm⁻¹), temperature (°C), and pressure (dbar).

If PSAL is already present in ds the function is a no-op.

Parameters:

ds (xarray.Dataset) – Dataset containing CNDC (conductivity, mS cm⁻¹), TEMP (temperature, °C), and PRES (pressure, dbar).

Returns:

Input dataset with PSAL added (same dimensions as CNDC), or unchanged if PSAL was already present.

Return type:

xarray.Dataset

oceanarray.analysis.hydrography.isopycnal_dataset(ds: Dataset, sigma_var: str = 'sigma0', sigma_grid: ndarray | None = None) → Dataset[source]

Build an isopycnal-tracking dataset from a gridded mooring file.

Tracks the pressure (and height above seabed) of density surfaces through time using the gridded sigma0 field. Calls isopycnal_pressure_series() column-by-column.

Parameters:

  • ds – Gridded mooring xr.Dataset with (pressure, time) dimensions and a sigma variable. A waterdepth global attribute (metres) is used for the height-above-seabed conversion; if absent both _height variables are all-NaN.

  • sigma_var – Name of the sigma variable in ds (default "sigma0").

  • sigma_grid – Target sigma0 values to track. If None, a 0.1 kg m⁻³ grid is computed from the observed data range.

Returns:

Dimensions (sigma0_level, time). Variables:

  • isopycnal_pressure — dbar, NaN where absent.

  • isopycnal_height — m above seabed, NaN where absent.

Return type:

xr.Dataset

oceanarray.analysis.hydrography.isopycnal_pressure_series(sigma0_tp: ndarray, pressure: ndarray, sigma_grid: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Find the pressure of each target density surface at every time step.

Uses a “first crossing from shallow” approach: for each target σ₀ value, scans from the shallowest pressure downward and finds the first level where sigma0 transitions from below to at-or-above the target, then linearly interpolates between those two levels. This is robust to non-monotonic sigma0 columns (which occur in gridded fields during knockdowns) and always returns the shallowest crossing — the physically meaningful pycnocline.

Returns NaN only when the target density is absent from the entire column (too light or too dense for any observed level at that time step).

Note

Operates on σ₀ (potential density referenced to 0 dbar). If the mooring was processed with a different reference pressure (e.g. σ₂ at 2000 dbar), pass the corresponding sigma variable. A future option --sig-ref / density_reference will generalise this; for now the variable name in the dataset controls which reference is used.

Parameters:

  • sigma0_tp – Shape (time, pressure). NaN where missing.

  • pressure – 1-D array of pressure levels in dbar. Need not be sorted — the function sorts each time step’s finite values by pressure before scanning for crossings.

  • sigma_grid – Target sigma0 values (kg m⁻³) at which to find the pressure.

Returns:

Shape (time, len(sigma_grid)). NaN where the target isopycnal is absent from the observed column at that time step.

Return type:

np.ndarray

spectral

Gonella rotary spectra, Welch PSD, and continuous wavelet transforms.

Spectral analysis utilities for oceanographic time series.

Provides rotary spectrum decomposition (Gonella 1972), Welch PSD estimates with and without gap-awareness, and continuous wavelet transforms.

Pairs with oceanarray.plotters.spectrum for figure output.

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.K1_PERIOD_DAYS: float = 0.9972695666666667

Period of the luni-solar diurnal tide K1, in days (23.93 h).

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.M2_PERIOD_DAYS: float = 0.51752505

Period of the principal lunar semidiurnal tide M2, in days (12.42 h).

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.SPECTRAL_MANY_LEVELS: int = 10

With at least this many candidate levels the temperature spectrum draws five lines instead of three.

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.SPECTRAL_MIN_FILLED: float = 0.9

Share of the record a grid level must have filled to carry a spectrum, wavelet or rotary spectrum line.

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.compute_cwt(x: ndarray, dt_seconds: float, wavelet: str = 'morlet', dj: float = 0.25, significance_level: float = 0.95) → dict[source]

Compute a continuous wavelet transform (CWT) on a 1-D time series.

Uses pycwt (Torrence & Compo 1998 method). The input array is gap-filled by linear interpolation before the transform; a boolean gap mask is returned so callers can overlay the filled regions.

If the AR(1) coefficient estimation fails (series too short or strongly trended), a WARNING is logged and the significance test falls back to a white-noise background (alpha=0); the wavelet itself is unaffected.

Parameters:

  • x – 1-D array of values. NaNs are treated as gaps and filled by linear interpolation before the transform.

  • dt_seconds – Sample interval in seconds.

  • wavelet – "morlet" (default, complex — gives amplitude and phase, best for oscillatory signals) or "mexican_hat" (real — better for detecting edges/sharp features, useful for wave-skewness studies).

  • dj – Fractional octave spacing between scales. Smaller values give more scales (finer period resolution) at higher compute cost. Default 0.25 (4 scales per octave).

  • significance_level – Confidence level for the chi-squared significance test against a red-noise background. Default 0.95 (95 %).

Returns:

  • dict with keys

  • - ``power`` (2-D array (n_scales, n_time), real wavelet power.)

  • - ``periods`` (1-D array of periods in **days*.*)

  • - ``coi`` (1-D array of raw record-edge COI periods in **days* (pycwt output).*)

  • - ``effective_coi`` (1-D array of gap-aware COI periods in **days*. At each time*) – step this is the minimum of the record-edge COI and the COI contributed by the nearest gap boundary. Inside gap columns it is 0 (entire period range unreliable). Use this for hatching in plots.

  • - ``signif`` (1-D array (n_scales,) — significance threshold for each) – scale; power > signif[:,None] is significant.

  • - ``gap_mask`` (boolean 1-D array (n_time,) — True where the original) – data was NaN (gap-filled region).

  • - ``dt_days`` (sample interval in days (convenience).)

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.gonella_rotary_spectrum(u_col: ndarray, v_col: ndarray, fs: float, nperseg: int, noverlap: int) → tuple[ndarray, ndarray, ndarray, ndarray][source]

Compute the Gonella (1972) rotary power spectrum from 1-D velocity components.

Both input arrays must be finite (no NaN). Calls scipy.signal.welch for the auto-spectra and scipy.signal.csd for the cross-spectrum, then applies the Gonella rotary decomposition.

Parameters:

  • u_col (np.ndarray) – 1-D east-velocity time series in m s⁻¹, finite (gap-filled).

  • v_col (np.ndarray) – 1-D north-velocity time series in m s⁻¹, finite (gap-filled).

  • fs (float) – Sampling frequency in cycles per day.

  • nperseg (int) – Number of samples per Welch segment.

  • noverlap (int) – Number of overlapping samples between adjacent Welch segments.

Returns:

(freq, s_cw, s_ccw, r) where:

  • freq — 1-D frequency array in cycles per day.

  • s_cw — clockwise power spectral density (≥ 0).

  • s_ccw — counter-clockwise power spectral density (≥ 0).

  • r — rotary coefficient (s_ccw - s_cw) / (s_ccw + s_cw), in [-1, 1]; 0 where both spectra are zero.

Return type:

tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

References

Gonella, J. (1972). A rotary-component method for analysing meteorological and oceanographic vector time series. Deep-Sea Research, 19(12), 833–846.

latitude (float or None) – Latitude in decimal degrees.

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.select_levels(data: ndarray, pressure: ndarray, *, at: ndarray | None = None, n: int | None = None, min_filled: float = 0.9) → list[int][source]

Return the grid levels a spectrum, wavelet or rotary spectrum is drawn at.

Candidates are the grid levels with values for at least min_filled of the record; when instrument pressures at are given, only the grid level nearest each instrument (within the grid) is a candidate. From the candidates, n are taken evenly from the shallowest to the deepest, so the shallowest and deepest are always included.

Parameters:

  • data (numpy.ndarray) – Values on (level, time); a level is filled where it is finite. For velocity pass a field that is NaN where either component is.

  • pressure (numpy.ndarray) – The grid levels (dbar), one per row of data, increasing.

  • at (numpy.ndarray or None, optional) – Instrument pressures (dbar). None: every grid level is a candidate.

  • n (int or None, optional) – How many levels to take. None: three, or five when there are at least SPECTRAL_MANY_LEVELS candidates.

  • min_filled (float, optional) – Share of the record a level must have filled (default SPECTRAL_MIN_FILLED).

Returns:

Level indices, shallowest first; all the candidates when there are no more than n.

Return type:

list of int

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.welch_psd(x: ndarray, dt_days: float, segment_length: int, overlap: float = 0.5, window: str = 'hann') → tuple[ndarray, ndarray][source]

Welch PSD estimate on a gap-filled (finite) time series.

Parameters:

  • x – 1-D array of evenly-spaced, finite values (no NaNs).

  • dt_days – Sample interval in days.

  • segment_length – Number of samples per Welch window (nperseg).

  • overlap – Fractional overlap between windows (default 0.5 → 50 %).

  • window – Window function name accepted by scipy.signal.welch.

Returns:

(frequencies_cpd, psd) where frequencies are in cycles per day.

Return type:

tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.welch_psd_gapaware(x: ndarray, dt_days: float, segment_length: int, overlap: float = 0.5, window: str = 'hann') → tuple[ndarray | None, ndarray | None, int][source]

Welch PSD over contiguous finite runs only; windows straddling gaps are skipped.

Returns a sample-count-weighted average PSD across all valid windows from all contiguous finite segments. This avoids the low-frequency bias that arises from gap-filling (linear interpolation) before the Welch estimate.

Switching the LF panel to gap-aware is a one-line change: replace welch_psd(col_filled, ...) with welch_psd_gapaware(col, ...).

Parameters:

  • x – 1-D array of evenly-spaced values; NaN marks gaps.

  • dt_days – Sample interval in days.

  • segment_length – Number of samples per Welch window (nperseg).

  • overlap – Fractional overlap between windows (default 0.5 → 50 %).

  • window – Window function name accepted by scipy.signal.welch.

Returns:

(frequencies_cpd, psd, n_windows) where n_windows is the total number of valid Welch windows used. Returns (None, None, 0) when no contiguous run is long enough for a single window.

Return type:

tuple[np.ndarray | None, np.ndarray | None, int]

oceanarray.analysis.spectral.welch_segment(n_time: int, dt_seconds: float, days: float, min_samples: int = 128) → int[source]

Return the Welch window length (samples) used for a days-long window.

The nominal window is days long. On a record too short for several such windows it is shortened to a quarter of the record (never below min_samples, nor longer than the record), so the estimate still averages a few windows.

Parameters:

  • n_time (int) – Number of samples in the record.

  • dt_seconds (float) – Sample interval in seconds.

  • days (float) – Nominal window length in days.

  • min_samples (int, optional) – Shortest window, in samples, when the window is shortened (default 128).

Returns:

Window length in samples (at least 2).

Return type:

int

Plotters

primitives

Tier-1 data-agnostic plot primitives (array-in / Figure-out).

Tier-1 data-agnostic plotting primitives.

These functions accept pre-processed arrays (not xarray Datasets) and have no knowledge of oceanographic variable naming conventions. They are the lowest layer in the three-tier plotters architecture:

Tier 1: primitives.py — generic, array-in / Figure-out Tier 2: _current.py etc. — domain wrappers (xr.Dataset-in / Figure-out) Tier 3: report/_plots.py — thin wrappers (path-in / base64-out)

Post-OdB: add plot_vector_heatmap, plot_section, plot_spectrum, plot_polar_histogram, plot_timeseries.

oceanarray.plotters.primitives.draw_trajectory(x: ndarray, y: ndarray, color_data: ndarray | None = None, cmap: str = 'coolwarm', xlabel: str = 'East displacement (m)', ylabel: str = 'North displacement (m)', colorbar_label: str = '', colorbar_unit: str = '', title: str = '', *, width_in: float = 4.5) → Figure[source]

Plot a 2D trajectory, optionally coloured per-segment by a scalar field.

When color_data is provided, segments are drawn as a LineCollection with colours mapped through cmap and a height-matched colorbar (unit as a title on top). When omitted, a plain line is drawn. Start and end are marked with green and red markers. The axes are laid out as an exact square via square_axes_grid() with square_limits(), so the colorbar height always matches the plotted square.

  • y (ndarray) – Trajectory coordinates (same length).

  • color_data (ndarray, optional) – Scalar values to map onto the line (same length as x/y).

  • cmap (str) – Matplotlib colormap name used when color_data is provided.

  • xlabel (str) – Axis labels.

  • ylabel (str) – Axis labels.

  • colorbar_label (str) – Fallback colorbar label placed on top when colorbar_unit is empty.

  • colorbar_unit (str) – Unit string placed above the colorbar (units-only on top, saves width).

  • title (str) – Figure title.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

oceanarray.plotters.primitives.hodograph_panel(ax: Any, e_v: ndarray, n_v: ndarray, t_frac: ndarray, title: str, units: str) → Any[source]

Draw a single velocity hodograph on a pre-squared ax; return its mappable.

Renders a time-coloured LineCollection trajectory (downsampled to <= 2 000 segments for performance) with start/end markers, symmetric -lim..lim limits, and a subtle grid. The panel does NOT draw its own colorbar — the caller owns one shared colorbar (all panels use the same 0->1 plasma time mapping); pass the returned ScalarMappable to unit_colorbar() on a shared cax from square_axes_grid().

e_v, n_v, and t_frac must already be filtered to the same finite-valid indices (no NaN, same length). ax is expected to be an exact square from square_axes_grid(); equal aspect is enforced with adjustable='datalim' so the box is never resized (which would strand the shared colorbar).

Parameters:

  • ax (matplotlib Axes) – Pre-squared target axes to draw on.

  • e_v (np.ndarray) – East and north velocity (finite values only, same length).

  • n_v (np.ndarray) – East and north velocity (finite values only, same length).

  • t_frac (np.ndarray) – Fractional deployment time 0 -> 1, same length as e_v.

  • title (str) – Axes title.

  • units (str) – Velocity unit string appended to axis labels, e.g. "m s^-1".

Returns:

The 0->1 plasma time mapping, for a shared colorbar.

Return type:

matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable

oceanarray.plotters.primitives.square_axes_grid(fig_w: float, nrows: int, ncols: int, *, colorbar: bool = True, per_panel_colorbar: bool = False, top_pad_in: float = 0.0, bottom_pad_in: float = 0.0, wgap_in: float | None = None, cbar_txt_in: float | None = None, left_in: float | None = None) → tuple[Figure, ndarray, Any][source]

Lay out an nrows × ncols grid of square axes, placed in inches.

Each panel is an exact square, so an equal-aspect plot fills it and a colorbar matches its height. Sets fig._manual_layout so the encoder skips tight_layout. Do not call set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box") on the axes: use symmetric limits or adjustable="datalim".

Parameters:

  • nrows (int) – Grid shape (≥ 1).

  • ncols (int) – Grid shape (≥ 1).

  • colorbar (bool, optional) – Reserve one shared colorbar axes on the right (ignored with per_panel_colorbar).

  • per_panel_colorbar (bool, optional) – One height-matched colorbar axes right of each panel.

  • top_pad_in (float, optional) – Extra inches above the title strip (e.g. for a suptitle).

  • bottom_pad_in (float, optional) – Extra inches below the x-tick strip.

  • wgap_in (float, optional) – Column gap (inches); smaller for panels sharing a y-axis.

  • cbar_txt_in (float, optional) – Width (inches) reserved for colorbar labels.

  • left_in (float, optional) – Left margin (inches) for y labels; see ytick_reserve_in().

Returns:

tuple of (matplotlib.figure.Figure, numpy.ndarray, object)

helpers

Shared colormap, normalisation, and style helpers used across Tier-2 modules.

Shared helpers for the plotters package.

Provides colormap helpers and rose-diagram rendering used across multiple Tier-2 plotter modules.

plotters/ never serialises to base64: the Tier-3 wrappers in reports/_plots.py encode each figure through the shared report encoder.

oceanarray.plotters.helpers.current_rose(ax: plt.Axes, east: np.ndarray, north: np.ndarray, *, title: str = '', n_dir: int = 16, cmap: str = 'Blues', r_max: float | None = None) → bool[source]

Draw a current rose on a polar Axes: the stack and grid pages’ one design.

Each wedge is a direction toward which the current flows (16 sectors, compass convention: north up, clockwise); its length is the percentage of the record in that direction, split into the speed classes ROSE_SPEED_CLASSES_CMS (light to dark). Rings are labelled in percent along the bearing where the wedges are shortest (that sector and its two neighbours), so the labels sit clear of the wedges.

Parameters:

  • ax (matplotlib.projections.polar.PolarAxes) – The target axes.

  • east (numpy.ndarray) – Velocity components (m s⁻¹), one value per time step.

  • north (numpy.ndarray) – Velocity components (m s⁻¹), one value per time step.

  • title (str, optional) – Panel title.

  • n_dir (int, optional) – Number of direction sectors (default 16).

  • cmap (str, optional) – Colormap of the speed classes (default "Blues").

  • r_max (float or None, optional) – The radial scale (%): one value for every rose of a figure (rose_max_percent()), so their rings compare; the rose’s own longest wedge when not given.

Returns:

False (and the axes hidden) when fewer than two values are present.

Return type:

bool

current

ADCP velocity plots: hodographs, current roses, stick plots, depth-time panels.

Tier-2 current and velocity figures: datasets in, Figures out (rendering in the Tier-1 primitives).

Roses (draw_instrument_rose(), draw_rose_grid(), draw_grid_rose(), draw_adcp_rose()), progressive vectors (draw_grid_progressive_vector()), hodographs (draw_adcp_hodograph(), draw_grid_hodograph()), ADCP sections (draw_adcp_velocity()) and Aquadopp tilt (draw_aquadopp_tilt_panels()).

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_adcp_hodograph(nc_path: str, lp_days: float = 4.0, smooth_hours: float = 24.0, *, width_in: float = 9.0) → Figure | None[source]

Two-depth hodograph for an ADCP per-instrument report; return a Figure.

Picks the bins nearest the 25th and 75th percentile of the valid range and renders a 2×2 figure: top row = far bin (75th pctile — typically shallower for upward-looking), bottom row = near bin (25th pctile). Left column = Tukey-smoothed raw; right column = eddy (LP mean removed). Returns None if east/north velocity are absent, 1-D, or too few valid bins.

Accepts both the current naming convention (east_velocity / north_velocity) and the legacy dolfyn names (u / v) so that files produced before the stage1 renaming was introduced can still be visualised. Files need to be regenerated with the current stage1 to get the canonical names.

Parameters:

  • nc_path (str) – Path to a stage-3 ADCP NetCDF file.

  • lp_days (float) – Low-pass filter cutoff in days for eddy extraction.

  • smooth_hours (float) – Tukey smoothing window in hours for the raw panel.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

Returns:

Figure, or None if velocity data are absent or insufficient.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

Progressive vector diagram of each ADCP bin, coloured by height above bottom.

Each depth bin integrated by Euler-forward from the origin. Bins whose every seabed_qc flag the mask_flags rule hides are omitted. Values the rule hides (oceanarray.pipeline.masking.masked()) count as zero velocity.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Stacked mooring dataset. ADCP bins are identified by instrument_type == "ADCP".

  • u_var (str) – Eastward and northward velocity variable names (m s⁻¹).

  • v_var (str) – Eastward and northward velocity variable names (m s⁻¹).

  • instr_type_var (str) – Coordinate variable names.

  • hab_var (str) – Coordinate variable names.

None if no ADCP bins are found.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None
