oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_adcp_velocity(nc_path: str, *, width_in: float = 9.0, rule: dict | None = None) → Figure | None[source]

Draw an ADCP’s stage-3 velocities as stacked time × range panels, for its instrument page.

One panel per variable present: east, north, up and error velocity (Spectral_r, symmetric at ±max(|p2|, |p98|) of the ENU velocities), current_speed (plasma, 0 to p98), current_direction (hsv, degrees toward which the water flows, clockwise from true north) and bin_pressure (viridis). Bins whose seabed_qc the mask_flags rule hides are masked. Range runs from 0 to the far edge of the last bin with data, inverted for a downward-looking ADCP.

Parameters:

  • nc_path (str) – The ADCP’s stage-3 file.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • rule (dict or None, optional) – The flag rule (mask_rules.resolve_mask_flags); the default when not given.

Returns:

None without velocity or range.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_aquadopp_speed_profile(ds: Dataset, speed_var: str = 'current_speed', u_var: str = 'east_velocity', v_var: str = 'north_velocity', instr_type_var: str = 'instrument_type', serial_var: str = 'serial', hab_var: str = 'hab', *, width_in: float = 4.5) → Figure | None[source]

Horizontal speed boxplots for all Aquadopps, one per instrument at its HAB.

X-axis: current speed. Y-axis: height above bottom (m). All Aquadopps appear on the same axes so the speed distribution can be compared across depths.

A level without a finite speed_var takes sqrt(u² + v²) from u_var and v_var; a level with neither is left out.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Stacked mooring dataset with shape (time, N_LEVELS).

  • speed_var (str) – Preferred speed variable name.

  • u_var (str) – Used to compute speed for a level where speed_var has none.

  • v_var (str) – Used to compute speed for a level where speed_var has none.

  • instr_type_var (str) – Dimension-coordinate variable names.

  • serial_var (str) – Dimension-coordinate variable names.

  • hab_var (str) – Dimension-coordinate variable names.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

Returns:

None if no Aquadopp level has a finite speed.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

Notes

Adapted from 02_aqdp_ploter.py by L. Moscatel (lmoscat), Universitat de Barcelona.

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_aquadopp_tilt_panels(ds: Dataset, *, step: int = 1, width_in: float = 9.0) → Figure | None[source]

One subplot per Aquadopp showing pitch, roll, and tilt_from_pressure.

Within each row the time-series panel and its paired scatter panel share one 0–90° y-axis, so the pitch/roll time series and the pressure-tilt scatter read on the same scale. Gridlines are drawn on both panels. Horizontal reference lines are drawn at the suspect and fail thresholds stored with the flags (tilt_limits()). A row without pitch or roll leaves its scatter panel blank.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – A stack with instrument_type, serial and hab on N_LEVELS and any of pitch, roll, tilt_from_pressure.

  • step (int, optional) – Plot every step-th time sample.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

Returns:

None if no Aquadopp level is found or none of the relevant variables exists.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_direction_profile_by_deployment(ds: Dataset, *, width_in: float = 4.5) → Figure | None[source]

Draw the current direction per velocity depth and deployment of a concatenated stack.

The companion of draw_speed_profile_by_deployment(): the same depths, flags and data rule, the same deployment colors and side-by-side placement. Direction is where the water flows to, degrees clockwise from true north. Each marker is the direction of the deployment’s mean velocity at that depth (from daily means, so tides do not count); its bar is the circular standard deviation of the daily-mean directions, stopped at the axis edge with an arrow where it runs past. An ADCP is drawn as a profile: per deployment, its bins’ direction against depth with that deviation shaded. The direction axis is centred on the mean direction of all depths and deployments, ±180°, so a flow near north is not split across 0°/360°.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – A concatenated stack (see draw_speed_profile_by_deployment()).

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches.

Returns:

None when no level has velocity.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_grid_hodograph(ds: Dataset, smooth_hours: float = 24.0, *, width_in: float = 9.0, levels: list[int] | None = None) → Figure | None[source]

Hodographs at grid levels for the grid report; return a Figure.

One square panel per level (two per row): the smooth_hours-smoothed east and north velocity traced through the deployment, coloured from start to end, with a circle at the start and a square at the end. By default the levels are those of the current roses (oceanarray.analysis.derived.velocity_levels()).

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – Gridded mooring dataset with east_velocity and north_velocity.

  • smooth_hours (float, optional) – Tukey smoothing window in hours (default 24).

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches (the display slot).

  • levels (list of int, optional) – Grid level indices (the page’s shared choice with the roses).

Returns:

None if velocity is absent or no level qualifies.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_grid_progressive_vector(ds: Dataset, *, width_in: float = 4.5) → Figure | None[source]

Progressive vector diagram at every grid level for the grid report.

For each pressure level, adds up the hourly velocity (Euler forward) into a cumulative displacement from the origin: how far water passing the mooring would travel if the flow were the same everywhere. It shows the mean flow direction and its steadiness, not the path of a water parcel. Returns None when east/north velocity are absent or all-NaN.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – Gridded dataset with dimensions (time, pressure), containing east_velocity and north_velocity in m s⁻¹.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_grid_rose(ds: Dataset, max_roses: int = 4, *, width_in: float = 9.0, levels: list[int] | None = None) → Figure | None[source]

Draw current roses at grid levels, in the stack page’s rose design.

One rose per level (oceanarray.plotters.helpers.current_rose()), titled with its pressure. By default the levels are those of oceanarray.analysis.derived.velocity_levels(): levels with velocity for at least half the record, at most max_roses, from the shallowest to the deepest.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – Gridded dataset with east_velocity and north_velocity (m s⁻¹) on (time, pressure).

  • max_roses (int, optional) – Most roses drawn when levels is not given (default 4).

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches (the display slot).

  • levels (list of int, optional) – Grid level indices to draw (the page’s shared choice).

Returns:

None when velocity is absent or no level qualifies.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_grid_trajectory(ds: Dataset, *, width_in: float = 4.5) → Figure | None

Former name of draw_grid_progressive_vector(), kept for callers.

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_hodograph(ds: Dataset, u_var: str = 'east_velocity', v_var: str = 'north_velocity', lp_days: float = 4.0, smooth_hours: float = 3.0, *, width_in: float = 9.0) → Figure[source]

Two-panel hodograph: Tukey-smoothed raw and eddy-only, coloured by time.

Panel 1: smooth_hours-Tukey-smoothed raw east-vs-north velocity. Panel 2: eddy component — raw minus a lp_days-day rolling-mean low-pass, then smooth_hours-Tukey smoothed to suppress instrument noise.

Points are coloured by fractional time through the record (0 = start, 1 = end) using a discrete viridis colorbar so the temporal evolution of rotary motion can be followed by eye. The figure title shows the instrument id from ds.attrs["id"] when available.

If u_var or v_var are absent, a placeholder figure is returned with an explanatory message — the caller always receives a renderable image.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Per-instrument dataset containing east and north velocity variables.

  • u_var (str) – Eastward velocity variable name (m s⁻¹).

  • v_var (str) – Northward velocity variable name (m s⁻¹).

  • lp_days (float) – Low-pass window length in days for the eddy-component panel.

  • smooth_hours (float) – Tukey smoothing window in hours applied to both panels.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_instrument_rose(nc_path: Path | Dataset, *, width_in: float = 9.0, title: str | None = None, rule: dict | None = None) → Figure | None[source]

Draw one instrument’s current roses in the stack page’s design; return Figure or None.

The good values’ rose (oceanarray.plotters.helpers.current_rose()), with the values rule hides left out, and beside it a rose of the values flagged suspect and one of those flagged bad, when there are any (rose_panels()). Each rose has its own ring scale: the flagged ones are small subsets. One speed-class legend.

Parameters:

  • nc_path (Path or xarray.Dataset) – The instrument’s stage-3 NetCDF file, or the file already open.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches (the display slot).

  • title (str or None, optional) – The rose’s title (the page’s "{serial} · {depth} m") when only the good rose is drawn; the serial when not given. With flagged roses each is titled by its values instead ("Suspect (originator): 246 values").

  • rule (dict or None, optional) – The flag rule (mask_rules.resolve_mask_flags); the default rule when not given.

Returns:

None without east and north velocity.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_multi_aquadopp_progressive_vector(ds: Dataset, u_var: str = 'east_velocity', v_var: str = 'north_velocity', temp_var: str = 'temperature', instr_type_var: str = 'instrument_type', serial_var: str = 'serial', title: str = '', *, width_in: float = 4.5) → Figure | None[source]

Progressive vector diagram of every Aquadopp, coloured by temperature.

Each line starts at the origin and adds up the measured east/north velocity over time (Euler forward; a missing velocity adds nothing): how far water passing the instrument would travel if the flow were the same everywhere. All trajectories share a single temperature colour scale so instruments can be compared directly. End points are annotated with the instrument serial.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Stacked mooring dataset with shape (time, N_LEVELS). Must contain instr_type_var, serial_var, u_var, v_var.

  • u_var (str) – Eastward and northward velocity variables (m s⁻¹).

  • v_var (str) – Eastward and northward velocity variables (m s⁻¹).

  • temp_var (str) – Temperature variable for colouring; omitted if not present in ds.

  • instr_type_var (str) – Dimension-coordinate variable names identifying each instrument.

  • serial_var (str) – Dimension-coordinate variable names identifying each instrument.

  • title (str) – Optional figure title; falls back to the dataset id attribute.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

Returns:

None if no Aquadopp instruments, or no east/north velocities, are found in the dataset.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

Notes

Adapted from 02_aqdp_ploter.py by L. Moscatel (lmoscat), Universitat de Barcelona.

Boxplot of current speed with printed percentile statistics.

Prints the 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 95th percentiles to stdout. NaN values are excluded before plotting.

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_speed_profile_by_deployment(ds: Dataset, *, width_in: float = 4.5) → Figure | None[source]

Current-speed box per velocity depth and deployment of a concatenated stack, overlaid.

Boxes of one depth sit at the depth’s nominal depth, one per deployment in its color (two consecutive deployments share a color, the second hatched), so a change in speed between deployments shows as boxes that do not overlap. An ADCP is drawn as a profile instead: per deployment, its bins’ median speed against depth with the middle 50 % shaded; the depth axis is labelled at the other instruments only. Values the mask_flags rule hides are left out, and a deployment’s box is drawn at a depth only when at least MIN_RECORD_FRACTION of that depth’s own steps in the deployment have valid velocity (a depth sampled for only part of the deployment is judged on its own record, not the whole window).

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – A concatenated stack, one column per depth, with east/north velocity, depth, serial (the depth’s label), cell_deployment(time, N_LEVELS) and deployment_name.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches.

Returns:

None when no level has velocity.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.current.draw_temperature_trajectory(ds: Dataset, u_var: str = 'east_velocity', v_var: str = 'north_velocity', temp_var: str = 'temperature', title: str = '') → object[source]

Lagrangian particle trajectory coloured per-segment by temperature.

Integrates u_var and v_var (east/north velocity) over time using a forward Euler scheme. NaN velocity values are treated as zero so the trajectory is not interrupted.

The displacement is in metres; for long deployments the trajectory will drift far from origin and should be interpreted as a pseudo-Lagrangian tracer, not a real particle path.

Note: the velocity integration step will move to oceanarray.analysis post-OdB so that it can be reused independently of plotting.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Dataset containing east/north velocity and temperature variables.

  • u_var (str) – Name of the eastward velocity variable (m s⁻¹).

  • v_var (str) – Name of the northward velocity variable (m s⁻¹).

  • temp_var (str) – Name of the temperature variable used for colouring.

  • title (str) – Optional figure title; defaults to the dataset id attribute.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure, or None when east/north velocity or temperature is absent.

oceanarray.plotters.current.progressive_vector(east_2d: ndarray, north_2d: ndarray, dt_s: ndarray, pressure: ndarray) → list[tuple[float, ndarray, ndarray]][source]

Compute pseudo-Lagrangian progressive-vector trajectories by pressure level.

Integrates east and north velocity time series using the Euler forward method to produce cumulative horizontal displacement from the origin. Levels with all-NaN velocity are silently skipped.

Parameters:

  • east_2d (np.ndarray) – East velocity array, shape (n_time, n_pressure) in m s⁻¹. NaN is treated as zero for the integration step in which it occurs.

  • north_2d (np.ndarray) – North velocity array, shape (n_time, n_pressure) in m s⁻¹. NaN is treated as zero for the integration step in which it occurs.

  • dt_s (np.ndarray) – 1-D array of time-step sizes in seconds, length n_time - 1.

  • pressure (np.ndarray) – 1-D pressure array of length n_pressure in dbar.

Returns:

One entry (p_val, x_km, y_km) per pressure level that has at least one finite velocity sample. p_val is the pressure in dbar; x_km and y_km are 1-D arrays of cumulative east and north displacement in km, length n_time.

Return type:

list of tuple[float, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Return an instrument rose’s panels: good, suspect and bad values apart.

A value’s flag is the worse of the originator’s and oceanarray’s for east and north velocity (marker_flags()). Good holds the values flagged neither suspect nor bad, less any rule hides; a suspect or bad panel is returned only when such values exist.

Returns:

(east, north, label, n) per panel, e.g. "Suspect (originator)" with its number of values; good first.

Return type:

list of (numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray, str, int)

oceanarray.plotters.timeseries.draw_grid_hydro(ds: xr.Dataset, var_bounds: dict | None = None, *, width_in: float = 9.0, instrument_pressures: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | Sequence[float] | None = None, scale: SectionScale | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Stacked temperature / salinity (PSU) sections for the grid report.

Each panel shows the variable on the pressure grid against time (surface up), over the levels with values, at the page’s vertical scale (scale). Colour limits are the 1st and 99th percentiles of the values unless var_bounds gives them; values beyond take the end colours (arrows on the colorbar). Instrument pressures are marked by triangles at the right edge.

Salinity: the salinity variable, or, when absent but conductivity and temperature are present, practical salinity from gsw.SP_from_C.

Parameters:

  • var_bounds (dict, optional) – Colour limits keyed "t_lim", "s_lim", "o2_lim" (each (vmin, vmax)), used instead of the percentiles.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches (the display slot).

  • instrument_pressures (Mapping of str to sequence of float, or sequence of float, optional) – Pressures (dbar) of the instruments behind each panel, keyed by variable (or one sequence for every panel); none marked when omitted.

  • scale (SectionScale, optional) – Vertical scale; default: the panels fill SECTION_AXES_IN.

Returns:

Figure, or None if no hydrographic data are present.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.timeseries.draw_grid_potential_density(ds: xr.Dataset, reference: str = 'sigma0', *, width_in: float = 9.0, derived: DerivedFields | None = None, density: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | None = None, scale: SectionScale | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

One potential-density section (σ0 or σ2) over the whole grid column.

σ is computed from potential temperature and practical salinity on the grid (oceanarray.analysis.derived.potential_density()), over the full column at one reference pressure. Colour limits are the 1st and 99th percentiles, with values beyond in the end colours.

  • reference ({"sigma0", "sigma2"}, optional) – The reference pressure: the surface (default) or 2000 dbar.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches (the display slot).

  • derived (DerivedFields or None, optional) – The page’s derived quantities (θ and the position), used when density is not given; computed from ds when neither is given.

  • density (Mapping of str to xarray.DataArray, optional) – σ0 and σ2 computed once for the page (oceanarray.analysis.derived.potential_density()), so the two sections share one computation.

  • scale (SectionScale, optional) – Vertical scale; default: that of ds’s hydrography.

Returns:

None when σ cannot be computed (no temperature, salinity or position).

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.timeseries.draw_grid_sigma(ds: xr.Dataset, *, width_in: float = 9.0) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Stacked sigma0 pcolormesh panel(s) for the stratification section.

Returns None when no sigma variables are present.

oceanarray.plotters.timeseries.draw_grid_timeseries(ds: xr.Dataset, *, width_in: float = 9.0, derived: DerivedFields | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Velocity time series at the depth of maximum time-mean current speed.

Two stacked panels (shared time axis):

  • Speed (black, m s⁻¹): sqrt(east² + north²); always ≥ 0.

  • East and North velocity (same axes, m s⁻¹): east in Okabe-Ito blue (#0072B2), north in Okabe-Ito orange (#E69F00). Both signed components are plotted together so the relationship between along- and cross-stream flow is immediately visible.

The target pressure level is chosen automatically as the level with the highest time-mean current speed and at least 70 % non-NaN coverage. The selected pressure is annotated in the figure title.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Gridded dataset with dimensions (time, pressure) containing at minimum east_velocity and north_velocity in m s⁻¹.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • derived (DerivedFields or None, optional) – The page’s derived quantities; its speed is used instead of being computed again.

Returns:

Figure, or None if horizontal velocity data are absent or all-NaN.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.timeseries.draw_grid_velocity_stacked(ds: xr.Dataset, *, width_in: float = 9.0, instrument_pressures: Sequence[float] | None = None, scale: SectionScale | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Velocity component, speed and direction sections for the grid report.

Eastward, northward and upward velocity, then current speed and the direction toward which the current flows. The panels are cropped to the levels with velocity and drawn at the page’s vertical scale (scale: the hydrography panels’ dbar per inch, so a dbar spans the same height in both figures), with the same pressure tick step. The three components share one colour scale, symmetric about zero, to the larger of the magnitudes of the 1st and 99th percentiles of all their values (values beyond take the end colours), and one colorbar spanning their panels. Speed (0 to its 98th percentile) and direction (a cyclic map, 0–360°) have their own colorbars.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – Gridded dataset with dimensions (time, pressure). Speed and direction are current_speed / current_direction when present, else computed from the horizontal components.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches (the display slot).

  • instrument_pressures (sequence of float, optional) – Pressures (dbar) of the current meters, marked by triangles at the right edge of each panel.

  • scale (SectionScale, optional) – Vertical scale; default: that of ds’s own hydrography (hydro_scale()).

Returns:

None when no velocity component is present or all are empty.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.timeseries.draw_stack_timeseries(ds: xr.Dataset, rows: list[tuple[str, str, bool, set[str] | None]], *, color_var: str, dot_overlay: bool = False, deployments: list[tuple[np.datetime64, np.datetime64, str]] | None = None, legend_shallow_first: bool = False, width_in: float = 9.0, label_lines: bool = False, row_heights: Sequence[float] | None = None, mark_suspect: bool = False, record: dict | None = None, keyed: Sequence[str] | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Stack time series: one row per variable, one line per instrument level.

The rows share the time axis and one instrument colour scheme (that of color_var, deep-first; see level_line_styles()), so a colour tracks an instrument through every row, and one legend on the right lists the instruments plotted. Values the stack’s mask_flags rule hides (ours or the originator’s flag; default 4) are left out. Long records are thinned to about 5000 points per line. The time axis spans time_coverage_start to time_coverage_end when the stack records them; with deployments (a site), the data drawn.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – A stack on (time, N_LEVELS) with serial and instrument_type on N_LEVELS.

  • rows (list of tuple) – (varname, ylabel, invert, exclude_types) per row; a variable not in ds is skipped, and instruments whose type is in exclude_types are not drawn in that row.

  • color_var (str) – The variable whose line colormap colours the instruments.

  • dot_overlay (bool, optional) – Also mark each sample with a dot (for sparse, spiky records).

  • deployments (list of (start, end, name), optional) – For a concatenated stack: each deployment’s window. The gaps between them are shaded, each boundary gets a thin line, and each deployment is named along the top.

  • legend_shallow_first (bool, optional) – List the levels shallowest first in the legend (the colors keep the deep-first order of ds).

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • label_lines (bool, optional) – Name each line by its serial at its right end in the first row (spread apart so they do not overlap) instead of a legend; instruments with no line in the first row get a small legend.

  • row_heights (sequence of float, optional) – Relative height of each row (e.g. a shorter upward-velocity row); equal rows when not given.

  • mark_suspect (bool, optional) – Mark the values flagged suspect (oceanarray’s or the originator’s flag) with small black dots.

  • record (dict or None, optional) – Filled with what was drawn: serials (the instruments with a line), labelled (those named at their line’s end), suspect (values marked) and legend (the serials in a legend).

  • keyed (sequence of str, optional) – Instruments already named on another figure of the page (the hydrography’s line labels): left out of the legend, so the legend lists only the others; with one instrument and nothing keyed, no legend (the caption names it).

Returns:

None when no row has an instrument with finite values.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.diagnostic.draw_knockdown_anomaly(ds: xr.Dataset, *, knockdown: Knockdown | None = None, width_in: float = 4.5) → matplotlib.figure.Figure | None[source]

IQR of pressure anomaly (measured − nominal) per instrument.

Each non-ADCP instrument is shown as a horizontal box-and-whisker at its nominal pressure on the y-axis; the box spans the IQR of the pressure anomaly distribution (actual − nominal, positive = knocked down deeper).

A vertical reference line at x = 0 marks zero knockdown. Box colour indicates the magnitude of the median knockdown:

Colour

Knockdown magnitude

green

< 100 dbar

gold

100–200 dbar

darkorange

200–300 dbar

firebrick

> 300 dbar

Interpolated pressure (QC flag 8) is excluded. Rendered at half-width in the stack report.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Stack dataset; same requirements as draw_knockdown_hab().

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • knockdown (oceanarray.analysis.derived.Knockdown or None, optional) – The stack’s knockdown inputs, built once per report and shared by the knockdown figures; built from ds when not given.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.diagnostic.draw_knockdown_displacement(ds: xr.Dataset, *, knockdown: Knockdown | None = None, width_in: float = 9.0) → matplotlib.figure.Figure | None[source]

Scatter and heatmap of estimated horizontal displacement vs. measured pressure.

For each non-ADCP instrument the horizontal displacement is estimated at every time step as:

x_horiz = sqrt(max(0, hab_nom² − hab_meas²))

where hab_nom is the nominal height-above-bottom (m) and hab_meas = waterdepth − depth(pressure) is the measured HAB, the measured pressure converted to depth (gsw.z_from_p) at the mooring’s latitude.

Left panel — scatter of (x_horiz, measured_pressure) per instrument, coloured by serial number. y-axis is measured pressure (dbar, increasing downward); x-axis is horizontal displacement (m). Square axes (equal aspect, adjustable data limits).

Right panel — 2-D count heatmap of the same points across all instruments combined. Discrete colorbar (up to 15 levels).

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Stack dataset; same requirements as draw_knockdown_hab().

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • knockdown (oceanarray.analysis.derived.Knockdown or None, optional) – The stack’s knockdown inputs, built once per report and shared by the knockdown figures; built from ds when not given.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.diagnostic.draw_knockdown_hab(ds: xr.Dataset, *, knockdown: Knockdown | None = None, width_in: float = 4.5) → matplotlib.figure.Figure | None[source]

IQR of measured pressure vs. nominal HAB, equal aspect ratio.

The y-axis is measured pressure (dbar, increasing downward).

Each non-ADCP instrument is shown as a vertical box-and-whisker positioned at its nominal HAB on the x-axis; the box spans the IQR of the measured pressure distribution. The dashed reference line shows the expected pressure for each HAB (pressure = waterdepth − hab). Boxes below the line were pulled deeper than their design height by current drag.

With 1 dbar ≈ 1 m, equal aspect keeps the reference line near 45° and the departure from it is directly related to horizontal displacement.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Stack dataset with dimensions (time, N_LEVELS) containing pressure, hab, serial, instrument_type, and optionally pressure_qc. The waterdepth global attribute must be present and non-zero.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • knockdown (oceanarray.analysis.derived.Knockdown or None, optional) – The stack’s knockdown inputs, built once per report and shared by the knockdown figures; built from ds when not given.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

Speed: p2.5–p97.5 and p25–p75 bands with the median (from east and north if current_speed is absent). East (#0072B2) and north (#E69F00): median and IQR. Count: time steps with a value per level.

  • scale (SectionScale or None, optional) – The page’s vertical scale (oceanarray.plotters.timeseries.hydro_scale()); default that of ds’s hydrography.

Returns:

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.diagnostic.draw_windows(nc_path: Path, instr_type: str, hours: int = 6, show_qc: bool = True, vlines: list | None = None, stage1_nc: Path | None = None, panels: list | None = None, *, width_in: float = 9.0, title: str | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Draw the combined start + end window figure: (nrows × 2) — left = first N h, right = last N h.

Parameters:

  • nc_path (Path) – Path to the processed (stage2 or stage3) NetCDF file.

  • instr_type (str) – Instrument type string (used in the figure title).

  • hours (int) – Width of each window in hours (default 6).

  • show_qc (bool) – Overlay QC flag markers on the data.

  • vlines (list of (time_val, color, label), optional) – Vertical marker lines to draw on both panels. time_val may be a numpy.datetime64, an ISO-8601 string, or a pandas.Timestamp. Lines are only drawn when they fall inside the plotted window. Labels appear as small rotated text at the top of the first row only to avoid excessive clutter.

  • stage1_nc (Path, optional) – Path to the stage1 NC file. When provided, the raw stage1 data is plotted as a light-grey background trace in each window panel so the full pre/post-deployment record is visible (bench → deployment in the left panel; deployment → recovery in the right panel). The x-axis limits are taken from the stage1 window extent so that the recovery transition appears even if the stage2/3 YAML trim cut it off. The y-axis limits are taken from the primary (stage2/3) data only so that bench-pressure outliers (p ≈ 0) do not squish the deployment-depth view.

  • panels (list, optional) – Subset of _instrument_panels tuples to draw. When given, only these rows are rendered (used to paginate a tall window figure across several images); otherwise every panel for the instrument is drawn on one figure.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • title (str or None, optional) – The figure title (the page’s "{Type} {serial} · {depth} m").

Returns:

Figure, or None if the dataset is too short to show windows.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

hydrography

T-S diagrams and isopycnal overlay figures.

Tier-2 domain wrappers for hydrographic section and isopycnal plots.

hydrography.py contains:

  • draw_isopycnal_ts: isopycnal height-above-seabed time series.

  • draw_isopycnal_coverage: three-panel isopycnal diagnostic.

  • draw_overflow_temperature: temperature time series at ~100 m above seabed.

Pairs with oceanarray.analysis.hydrography for density computations.

oceanarray.plotters.hydrography.COVERAGE_FAIR_PCT: float = 50.0

Isopycnal coverage (% of time steps) at or above which a σ₀ bar is amber, below COVERAGE_GOOD_PCT; red below this.

oceanarray.plotters.hydrography.COVERAGE_GOOD_PCT: float = 80.0

Isopycnal coverage (% of time steps) at or above which a σ₀ bar is green; the dashed reference line of the coverage panel.

oceanarray.plotters.hydrography.draw_isopycnal_coverage(ds: xr.Dataset, *, width_in: float = 9.0) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Three-panel isopycnal diagnostic; return a Figure.

Panel 0 — Distribution: horizontal histogram of all gridded σ₀ values (all time steps × all pressure levels), binned at 0.1 kg m⁻³. Shows how the water column is distributed in density space.

Panel 1 — Coverage: for each σ₀ value at 0.1 kg m⁻³ spacing, the percentage of valid time steps during which the target surface lies within the measured column (min(sigma0_column) ≤ target ≤ max(sigma0_column)). Colour-coded: green at or above COVERAGE_GOOD_PCT, amber from COVERAGE_FAIR_PCT up to it, red below; dashed reference line at COVERAGE_GOOD_PCT.

Panel 2 — Depth distribution: for each target surface, the median height above seabed (or pressure when waterdepth or the latitude is unavailable), with the IQR (25th–75th percentile) as a thick bar and the 5th–95th percentile as a thin whisker.

The shared y-axis (σ₀) is clipped to the 2.5th–99.99th percentile of the distribution — this removes rare light-water outliers from the top while retaining all of the dense water at the bottom. Currently selected params.SIGMA_GRID targets are marked with orange diamonds (panel 1) and dotted guide lines (panel 2).

Parameters:

  • ds – Gridded mooring xr.Dataset containing a variable whose name starts with "sigma" and has pressure and time dimensions.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

Returns:

Figure, or None if required sigma data are absent.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

Plots a 1-hour running median of each σ₀ surface’s height above seabed. NaN gaps break the line naturally (pandas rolling preserves NaN boundaries). Colormap: Blues — light blue = lower density (shallower), dark = denser (deeper).

Parameters:

Returns:

Figure, or None if required data are absent.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

Selects the grid pressure level nearest to 100 dbar above the seabed pressure (the water depth converted to pressure at the mooring latitude) and plots a 1-hour running median temperature time series. Returns None if waterdepth is missing, temperature is absent, or all values are NaN.

spectrum

Power spectra and rotary spectrum figures.

Tier-2 spectral figures: Welch spectra, wavelet scalograms and rotary spectra of a grid.

Computations are in oceanarray.analysis.spectral.

oceanarray.plotters.spectrum.draw_grid_rotary_spectrum(ds: xr.Dataset, lat: float = 0.0, *, width_in: float = 9.0, levels: Sequence[int] | None = None, markers: Sequence[tuple[str, float]] = ()) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Two-panel rotary velocity spectrum for the grid report; return a Figure.

Left panel: CW (solid, reds) and CCW (dashed, blues) power spectra on the same axes, one line per selected pressure level. Right panel: rotary coefficient r = (CCW - CW) / (CCW + CW) on a linear [-1, 1] scale. Welch PSD with Hann window, 14-day segments (shortened on a short record, oceanarray.analysis.spectral.welch_segment()), 50% overlap. Vertical lines mark M2, K1, the inertial period and any markers.

Levels: levels, else three from those with both components for at least SPECTRAL_MIN_FILLED of the record (oceanarray.analysis.spectral.select_levels()).

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Gridded dataset with east_velocity and north_velocity on (time, pressure) dimensions.

  • lat (float) – Mooring latitude (degrees, positive north) used for the inertial period marker.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • levels (sequence of int, optional) – Pressure-level indices to draw (the page’s choice).

  • markers (sequence of (str, float), optional) – Extra (label, period in days) markers.

Returns:

Figure, or None if insufficient velocity data.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.spectrum.draw_spectrum(da_temp: xr.DataArray, dt_seconds: float, lat: float = 0.0, hf_segment_days: float = 7.0, hf_x_max_days: float = 2.0, *, width_in: float = 9.0, lf_segment_days: float = 14.0, levels: Sequence[int] | None = None, markers: Sequence[tuple[str, float]] = ()) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Two-panel Welch spectrum of gridded temperature at a few levels.

Left: lf_segment_days Hann windows over all periods the windows resolve. Right: hf_segment_days Hann windows, zoomed to periods shorter than hf_x_max_days. Both 50 % overlap; on a record too short for several windows the windows are shortened (oceanarray.analysis.spectral.welch_segment()). The left panel gap-fills by linear interpolation before the estimate; the right uses only windows within unbroken runs of values. Lines are coloured by pressure (colour bar); vertical lines mark M2, K1, the inertial period and any markers; a dashed −2 slope is drawn for reference.

Parameters:

  • da_temp (xarray.DataArray) – Gridded temperature with dimensions pressure and time.

  • dt_seconds (float) – Uniform time step of the grid in seconds.

  • lat (float, optional) – Mooring latitude in decimal degrees, for the inertial period; 0 omits it.

  • hf_segment_days (float, optional) – Window length of the right panel in days (default 7).

  • hf_x_max_days (float, optional) – Longest period shown in the right panel in days (default 2); at most 3 puts that axis in hours.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches (the display slot).

  • lf_segment_days (float, optional) – Window length of the left panel in days (default 14).

  • levels (sequence of int, optional) – Pressure-level indices to draw (the page’s choice); default oceanarray.analysis.spectral.select_levels() on all grid levels.

  • markers (sequence of (str, float), optional) – Extra (label, period in days) markers.

Returns:

None when no level has enough values.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.spectrum.draw_wavelet(da_temp: xr.DataArray, dt_seconds: float, wavelet: str = 'morlet', *, width_in: float = 9.0, levels: Sequence[int] | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

Continuous wavelet transform scalogram for gridded temperature; return a Figure.

Produces up to three stacked wavelet + time-series panel pairs, at the outermost levels with values for at least SPECTRAL_MIN_FILLED of the record and one between (oceanarray.analysis.spectral.select_levels()), unless levels names them. The period axis starts at six time steps, and never below 2 hours. Columns gap-filled before the transform are cross-hatched.

Each wavelet panel shows log10(Morlet power) as a filled contour plot; the gap-aware cone of influence (COI) is hatched – this covers both the record edges and the COI wings that spread out from every data gap. The y-axis is trimmed per-panel to the longest period that is reliable at any time step, so gappier levels automatically get a tighter period range. A 95 % significance contour is drawn in black (falls back to white-noise background if AR(1) estimation fails). Below each wavelet panel a short temperature time series for that depth level shares the x-axis.

Parameters:

  • da_temp – Gridded temperature DataArray with dimensions (pressure, time).

  • dt_seconds – Sample interval in seconds.

  • wavelet – "morlet" (default, Morlet omega_0=6) or "mexican_hat".

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • levels (sequence of int, optional) – Pressure-level indices to draw (at most three are used).

Returns:

Figure, or None if the dataset has insufficient temperature data.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.spectrum.spectrum_markers(lat: float | None, extra: Sequence[tuple[str, float]] = ()) → list[tuple[str, float, str]][source]

Return the frequency markers of the spectra: M2, K1, the inertial period, extra.

Parameters:

  • lat (float or None) – Mooring latitude (degrees); no inertial marker when None or 0.

  • extra (sequence of (str, float), optional) – Further (label, period in days) markers (the mooring YAML’s spectrum_markers).

Returns:

(label, period in days, colour).

Return type:

list of (str, float, str)

oceanarray.plotters.spectrum.wavelet_panel(ax: matplotlib.axes.Axes, times: np.ndarray, periods: np.ndarray, power: np.ndarray, coi: np.ndarray, signif: np.ndarray | None = None, title: str = '', *, gap_mask: np.ndarray | None = None, min_period: float | None = None) → mcolors.ScalarMappable[source]

Draw one wavelet scalogram panel onto ax.

Renders log10(power) as a filled contour plot with period on a log y-axis (inverted so short periods are at the top), time on x.

The COI region (period > coi[t]) is hatched with diagonal lines. Callers should pass effective_coi from compute_cwt rather than the raw pycwt COI — the effective COI already incorporates gap-edge wings so that one hatching call covers record edges, gap columns, and the surrounding unreliable region.

The y-axis is trimmed to coi.max() so entirely-hatched long-period rows are not shown; gappier records automatically get a tighter period range.

An optional 95 % significance contour is drawn in black.

Parameters:

  • ax – Target axes object.

  • times – 1-D array of time values (any type accepted by matplotlib, e.g. numpy datetime64 or float index).

  • periods – 1-D array of wavelet periods in days (length n_scales).

  • power – 2-D array of real wavelet power, shape (n_scales, n_time).

  • coi – 1-D array of COI periods in days, length n_time. Pass effective_coi from compute_cwt to include gap-edge wings.

  • signif – Optional 1-D significance threshold array, length n_scales. Where power[i, t] > signif[i] the transform is significant at the chosen confidence level. If None, no significance contour is drawn.

  • title – Axes title string (e.g. depth label).

  • gap_mask – Optional boolean array, length n_time: True where the series was gap-filled before the transform; those columns are cross-hatched.

  • min_period – Shortest period shown (days); default the shortest computed.

Returns:

Mappable suitable for passing to fig.colorbar().

Return type:

matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable

oceanarray.plotters.ts.draw_grid_ts_diagram(ds: xr.Dataset, n_bins: int = 60, *, width_in: float = 9.0, derived: DerivedFields | None = None) → tuple[plt.Figure, dict] | None[source]

T-S diagram for gridded mooring data; return a (Figure, bounds_dict) tuple.

Left panel: 2-D count heatmap (log₁₀ samples per T-S bin). Right panel (when oxygen_saturation_pct is present): median O₂ saturation per T-S bin, computed with scipy.stats.binned_statistic_2d. Bins with fewer than 5 samples are masked white.

This lets you see which water masses (T-S combinations) are oxygen-rich vs oxygen-depleted at this mooring — a compact water-mass characterisation.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Gridded dataset with at least temperature and salinity variables.

  • n_bins (int) – Number of bins per axis for the 2-D histogram.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • derived (DerivedFields or None, optional) – The page’s derived quantities (position, θ), computed once by the report; read from ds when not given.

Returns:

The T-S axes are potential temperature (σθ contours) when the position is known, else in-situ temperature. bounds_dict contains the axis/colorbar limits computed from the data so the hydro pcolormesh panels can share the same scales:

  • "t_lim" : (vmin, vmax) for in-situ temperature

  • "s_lim" : (vmin, vmax) for salinity

  • "o2_lim" : (vmin, vmax) for oxygen_saturation_pct, or None

  • "sigma_interval" : the σθ contour interval (kg m⁻³), or None without contours

Return type:

tuple of (plt.Figure, bounds_dict) or None

oceanarray.plotters.ts.draw_stack_ts_diagram(ds: xr.Dataset, *, width_in: float = 9.0, derived: DerivedFields | None = None, record: dict | None = None, full_range: bool = False) → plt.Figure | None[source]

T-S diagram for a stacked dataset; return a Figure.

Scatter-by-pressure, count heatmap, and (when present) scatter-by-AOU. Panels are arranged in a single row. The AOU panel is included when apparent_oxygen_utilization is present in ds (written by stage3 for instruments with dissolved oxygen data).

QC masking: values the mask_flags rule hides are left out (the rule the stack records, else the default).

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Stacked mooring dataset containing temperature and salinity.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • derived (DerivedFields or None, optional) – The page’s derived quantities (position, θ), computed once by the report; read from ds when not given.

  • record (dict or None, optional) – Filled with what was drawn: theta, sigma_interval, no_sigma (why σθ is not drawn, or None), colour ("pressure" or None) and oxygen (bool).

  • full_range (bool, optional) – Axes over every value (the Stack cat), not the 1–99 % range.

Returns:

Figure, or None if temperature or salinity are absent. The y-axis is potential temperature with σθ contours when the position is known, in-situ temperature without contours otherwise.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.ts.draw_ts_by_deployment(ds: xr.Dataset, *, width_in: float = 4.5, derived: DerivedFields | None = None, record: dict | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

T-S of a concatenated stack by deployment: an outline and a median per instrument level.

For each depth and deployment with at least TS_MIN_LEVEL_POINTS points of temperature and salinity, the outline encloses TS_OUTLINE_FRACTION of that level’s points (the densest region of its T-S histogram, smoothed over 3 × 3 bins), and a dot marks its median S and T. With more than TS_MAX_OUTLINES such levels the outlines are left out and only the medians and lines are drawn. A line joins each deployment’s medians in pressure order (levels within TS_COLOCATED_DBAR averaged): a guide to the eye along the profile, not interpolated data. Two consecutive deployments share a color; the second has dashed outlines and line and a square marker. Values the Stack cat’s mask_flags rule hides are left out. A shift between the deployments at the same depth is what this panel is for.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – A concatenated stack, one column per depth (time, N_LEVELS), with temperature, salinity, cell_deployment(time, N_LEVELS) (the deployment behind each value, -1 none) and deployment_name(DEPLOYMENT); pressure orders the median line (else the column order).

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches.

  • derived (DerivedFields or None, optional) – The page’s derived quantities (position, θ), computed once by the report; read from ds when not given. The y-axis is potential temperature with σθ contours when the position is known, else in-situ temperature.

  • record (dict or None, optional) – Filled with levels (levels drawn), outlines (bool) and sigma_interval.

Returns:

None without temperature, salinity or the deployment record, or when no level has enough data.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.ts.draw_ts_diagram(nc_path: Path, *, width_in: float = 9.0, derived: DerivedFields | None = None, flag_sources: tuple[str, ...] | None = None, record: dict | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

T-S diagram from a NetCDF path; return a Figure.

Scatter by pressure, 2-D count heatmap, and (when present) scatter by O2 saturation: the stack page’s figure for one instrument. Every value is drawn; values flagged suspect (dots) or bad (crosses), in the worse of the flag sets read, are marked on the left panel. The pressure colour bar runs shallow at the top; σθ contours are labelled inside the axes.

Parameters:

  • nc_path (Path) – Path to a stage-3 NetCDF file.

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width (inches), the report slot; default the full content width.

  • derived (DerivedFields or None, optional) – The page’s derived quantities (position, θ); read from the file when not given.

  • flag_sources (tuple of str or None, optional) – Flag-variable suffixes read for the markers (default oceanarray’s and the originator’s).

  • record (dict or None, optional) – Filled with what was drawn: theta, sigma_interval, colour ("pressure" or "sample"), oxygen, counts (values marked per flag).

Returns:

Figure, or None if temperature or salinity are absent. The y-axis is potential temperature with σθ contours when the position is known, in-situ temperature without contours otherwise.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.ts.draw_ts_points_by_deployment(ds: xr.Dataset, *, width_in: float = 4.5, derived: DerivedFields | None = None, record: dict | None = None) → plt.Figure | None[source]

T-S point cloud of a concatenated stack, one color per deployment, thinned.

At most TS_MAX_POINTS values per deployment, picked at random with a fixed seed (TS_POINTS_SEED), so years of hourly values do not bury one another and the page is the same each time it is drawn. Values the Stack cat’s mask_flags rule hides are left out. Deployments are drawn in random order, point by point, so none sits on top of all the others.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – A concatenated stack, one column per depth (time, N_LEVELS), with temperature, salinity, cell_deployment(time, N_LEVELS) (the deployment behind each value, -1 none) and deployment_name(DEPLOYMENT).

  • width_in (float, optional) – Figure width in inches.

  • derived (DerivedFields or None, optional) – The page’s derived quantities (position, θ), computed once by the report; read from ds when not given. The y-axis is potential temperature with σθ contours when the position is known, else in-situ temperature.

  • record (dict or None, optional) – Filled with sigma_interval.

Returns:

None without temperature, salinity or the deployment record, or with no value left.

Return type:

plt.Figure or None

oceanarray.plotters.ts.sigma0_contours(s_lim: tuple[float, float], t_lim: tuple[float, float], position: tuple[float, float] | None, n_grid: int = 200) → SigmaContours | None[source]

Return the σθ contours for a T-S figure, from its shared axis limits.

The contours are at whole multiples of a round interval (0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 kg m⁻³) chosen to give four to ten lines across the panel. Every panel of the figure draws the same grid (draw_sigma0_contours()).

Parameters:

  • s_lim (tuple of float) – The figure’s practical-salinity and potential-temperature axis limits.

  • t_lim (tuple of float) – The figure’s practical-salinity and potential-temperature axis limits.

  • position (tuple of (float, float) or None) – (latitude, longitude) of the mooring; no contours when None.

  • n_grid (int, optional) – Grid points along each axis.

Returns:

None without a position, or when the limits or σθ are not finite (logged at debug level).

Return type:

SigmaContours or None

animation

Animated GIF output via matplotlib.animation.

Animated plot functions for the oceanarray plotters package.

This module is intentionally separate from the static (Tier-1/2/3) pipeline. It relies on matplotlib.animation and requires the pillow package as a GIF writer. scipy is required for the Tukey smoothing window.

Future interactive equivalents (plotly, bokeh) should live in a companion interactive.py module so the animation and interactive layers stay clearly distinct.

Tier classification: Tier-2 domain functions (xr.Dataset-in / file-out).

oceanarray.plotters.animation.animate_hodograph(ds: Dataset, output_path: str | Path, u_var: str = 'east_velocity', v_var: str = 'north_velocity', lp_days: float = 4.0, smooth_hours: float = 3.0, frame_hours: float = 6.0, fps: int = 20, dpi: int = 100) → Path | None[source]

Write an animated GIF of the smoothed hodograph drawing itself through time.

Each frame advances by frame_hours of real deployment time and reveals the smoothed velocity trajectory accumulated up to that moment, so the viewer watches rotary/eddy structure build up through the record.

Signal processing (applied once to the full record before animating):

  • Raw panel — smooth_hours-Tukey filter of the raw east/north signal.

  • Eddy panel — lp_days-day rolling-mean removed, then smooth_hours- Tukey filter to suppress instrument noise.

A timestamp header on each frame shows the real date and time.

Requires pillow (pip install pillow) as the GIF writer and scipy for the Tukey window.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset) – Per-instrument dataset with east/north velocity variables and a time dimension.

  • output_path (str or Path) – Destination file path; .gif extension recommended.

  • u_var (str) – Eastward velocity variable name (m s⁻¹).

  • v_var (str) – Northward velocity variable name (m s⁻¹).

  • lp_days (float) – Low-pass window length in days for the eddy-component panel.

  • smooth_hours (float) – Tukey smoothing window in hours applied to both panels.

  • frame_hours (float) – Time step between frames in hours (default 6 h → one frame per quarter-day of deployment).

  • fps (int) – Frames per second in the output GIF.

  • dpi (int) – Resolution of each frame in dots per inch.

Returns:

  • Path – The resolved output path on success.

  • None – If u_var or v_var are absent from ds, or if the pillow writer is unavailable.
